topic: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults LADA: GAD antibodies, insulin progression

guidelinesKept: Management of Latent Autoimmune Diabetes in Adults: A Consensus Statement From an International Expert Panel

page.mentor_intro: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA) presents phenotypically as type 2 diabetes but features islet autoantibodies and progressive immune-mediated pancreatic beta-cell destruction. Clinical decision-making balances early glycemic control with beta-cell preservation, guided by baseline GADA titers and residual C-peptide secretion.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 international expert consensus on LADA establishes that screening for glutamic acid decarboxylase autoantibodies (GADA) is recommended in adults presenting with apparent type 2 diabetes who are non-obese, age under 50, or exhibit early oral agent failure.

Residual fasting C-peptide concentrations stratify therapeutic pathways in LADA: levels below 0.3 nmol/L require an immediate multiple-dose insulin regimen, while levels from 0.3 to 0.7 nmol/L represent a vulnerable gray zone where insulin is introduced or combined with incretin therapies.

Sulfonylureas are contraindicated or strongly discouraged in LADA as secretagogues accelerate autoimmune beta-cell apoptosis and hasten progression toward complete insulin dependence compared to insulin or metformin.

Longitudinal follow-up demonstrates that high-titer GADA positivity confers a significantly faster rate of beta-cell loss, with over 50% requiring absolute insulin replacement within 3 to 6 years of clinical diagnosis.

guidelinesKept: Updated Guidelines for the Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection: CDC and National Tuberculosis Controllers Association

page.mentor_intro: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) represents a state of persistent immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens without evidence of clinically active disease. Clinical management prioritizes identifying high-risk individuals for progression, excluding active pulmonary or extrapulmonary disease, and selecting short-course rifamycin regimens.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 CDC and NTCA guidelines preferentially recommend short-course rifamycin-based regimens over 6- to 9-month isoniazid monotherapy for treating latent tuberculosis infection due to superior completion rates and reduced hepatotoxicity.

Active tuberculosis disease must be definitively excluded via targeted symptom screening and chest radiography before commencing any latent TB regimen to prevent the rapid emergence of rifamycin resistance.

Interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) demonstrate superior diagnostic specificity over the tuberculin skin test (TST) in individuals with prior BCG vaccination or non-tuberculous mycobacterial exposures.

The randomized PREVENT TB trial confirmed that 3 months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP) is noninferior to 9 months of daily isoniazid, with treatment completion rates of 82.1% versus 69.0%.

guidelinesKept: Updated Guidelines for the Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection: CDC and National Tuberculosis Controllers Association

page.mentor_intro: Latent tuberculosis infection treatment prevents progression to active disease in high-risk hosts. Modern guidelines prioritize 3- to 4-month rifamycin-containing options (3HP, 4R, 3HR) over protracted isoniazid monotherapies, balancing cytochrome P450 interactions and hepatic tolerance.

teaching_points.claim: The preferred first-line options for latent tuberculosis in the 2020 CDC/NTCA guidelines are 3 months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP) or 4 months of daily rifampin monotherapy (4R).
Daily rifampin for 4 months (4R) offers a favorable safety profile with significantly lower drug-induced liver injury (0.3% vs 2.5%) and higher adherence compared to 9 months of daily isoniazid (9H).

Rifamycins are potent inducers of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, necessitating close dosage adjustment or alternative regimens for patients taking protease inhibitors, direct oral anticoagulants, or calcineurin inhibitors.
In patients with HIV receiving efavirenz or dolutegravir-based ART, 3HP can be safely co-administered with appropriate dose adjustments, expanding access to short-course curative therapy.

topic: Late-onset hypogonadism: diagnostic thresholds, testosterone replacement risks, monitoring

guidelinesKept: Testosterone Therapy in Men with Hypogonadism: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline

page.mentor_intro: Late-onset hypogonadism involves persistent clinical features of androgen deficiency paired with unequivocally low serum testosterone levels in aging men. The Endocrine Society emphasizes rigorous morning laboratory verification, exclusion of reversible secondary etiologies, and objective cardiovascular risk evaluation.

teaching_points.claim: The Endocrine Society clinical guideline requires at least two separate fasting morning (8:00 AM to 10:00 AM) total testosterone measurements below 300 ng/dL (10.4 nmol/L) alongside specific clinical symptoms to establish a diagnosis of hypogonadism.

The randomized TRAVERSE trial of 5,246 hypogonadal men with cardiovascular disease or high risk showed that transdermal testosterone therapy was noninferior to placebo for major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.96; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.17).

In the TRAVERSE trial, testosterone therapy did not reduce clinical fracture risk and was unexpectedly associated with a numerically higher incidence of all clinical fractures compared with placebo (HR 1.43).

Baseline and surveillance monitoring during testosterone replacement requires periodic hematocrit assessment to detect polycythemia, with treatment withholding or dose reduction recommended if hematocrit exceeds 54%.

topic: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow): assessment and management
cluster: lateral epicondylitis tennis elbow assessment and management

page.mentor_intro: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) is a chronic angiofibroblastic tendinopathy of the common extensor origin, primarily involving the extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB). Management focuses on eccentric wrist extensor rehabilitation, while reserving interventional therapies for refractory pain.

teaching_points.claim: A landmark randomized trial in JAMA demonstrated that corticosteroid injection provides superior short-term pain relief at 4 weeks but is associated with significantly higher recurrence rates and worse 1-year outcomes compared to physiotherapy or wait-and-see.

A randomized controlled trial in the BMJ demonstrated that physical therapy combining elbow mobilization with movement and eccentric exercise yields superior durable long-term success at 52 weeks compared with corticosteroid injection.

A 2023 meta-analysis of Level 1 and 2 randomized trials established that corticosteroid injections are superior to platelet-rich plasma (PRP) at 1 month, whereas PRP achieves superior and durable functional and pain scores at 6 months.

Pathologically, lateral epicondylitis represents non-inflammatory angiofibroblastic tendinosis and collagen disorientation rather than acute inflammation, explaining the limited disease-modifying utility of chronic oral NSAIDs.

topic: latest guideline recommendations for atrial fibrillation stroke prevention

guidelinesKept: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the Management of Atrial Fibrillation Developed in Collaboration with EACTS

page.mentor_intro: Stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation is centered on risk stratification and oral anticoagulation. The 2024 ESC guidelines introduced the CHA2DS2-VA score and reiterated the primacy of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) over vitamin K antagonists in non-valvular disease.

teaching_points.claim: The 2024 ESC guidelines for atrial fibrillation introduced the CHA2DS2-VA score, removing female sex as an independent score point and establishing oral anticoagulation as strongly indicated for scores of 2 or higher.

Direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban) are class I recommended over vitamin K antagonists (warfarin) in non-valvular atrial fibrillation due to superior reductions in intracranial hemorrhage and mortality.
Warfarin remains the mandatory anticoagulant of choice in patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic heart valves, where DOACs are contraindicated.

In patients with a CHA2DS2-VA score of 1 in men or equivalent clinical risk, oral anticoagulation should be considered (Class IIa), balancing individual bleeding risk using modifiable risk factor calculators.

guidelinesKept: Management of Suspected Immediate Perioperative Allergic Reactions: An International Overview and Consensus Recommendations

page.mentor_intro: Perioperative anaphylaxis requires immediate resuscitation and multidisciplinary allergological investigation. The 2019 international consensus recommendations establish protocols for acute serial tryptase measurements, identification of latex vs drug triggers, and timing of diagnostic skin testing.

teaching_points.claim: The 2019 international consensus recommendations emphasize that immediate management of perioperative anaphylaxis requires prompt intramuscular or titrated intravenous epinephrine alongside aggressive crystalloid resuscitation.

Serial serum total tryptase sampling is recommended at the time of resuscitation, at 1 to 2 hours post-reaction, and at baseline (after at least 24 hours) to confirm mast cell activation via the consensus formula: acute tryptase > (1.2 x baseline tryptase + 2 ug/L).

Comprehensive allergy workup including skin prick testing and specific IgE testing should be scheduled 4 to 6 weeks following the acute episode to avoid false-negative results from transient mast cell exhaustion.

High-risk populations for Type I IgE-mediated latex allergy include patients with spina bifida, congenital urological anomalies with multiple surgical exposures, healthcare workers, and individuals with latex-fruit syndrome (banana, avocado, kiwi, chestnut).

guidelinesKept: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the Management of Dyslipidaemias: Lipid Modification to Reduce Cardiovascular Risk

page.mentor_intro: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk reduction is fundamentally driven by absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction. Landmark trials and current guidelines establish that lower LDL-C levels achieved over long durations yield progressive reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events without an identified lower safety threshold.

teaching_points.claim: The IMPROVE-IT trial established that adding ezetimibe to simvastatin in post-acute coronary syndrome patients lowered median LDL-C to 53.7 mg/dL and significantly reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.936, P=0.016), validating non-statin LDL lowering.

The FOURIER trial demonstrated that adding the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab to statin therapy lowered LDL-C to a median of 30 mg/dL and significantly reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, hospitalization for angina, or revascularization (HR 0.85, P<0.001).

The ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trial confirmed that alirocumab added to high-intensity statin therapy after acute coronary syndrome significantly reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.85) and was associated with lower all-cause mortality in patients with baseline LDL-C >= 100 mg/dL.

The 2019 ESC/EAS guidelines establish an intensive LDL-C goal of <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) alongside at least a 50% baseline reduction for individuals at very high cardiovascular risk, recommending a stepwise addition of ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors.

guidelinesKept: 2021 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis & AAO Screening Recommendations

page.mentor_intro: Conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) form the cornerstone of inflammatory arthritis management. Safe clinical use demands vigilance for unique organ toxicities: irreversible retinal maculopathy with hydroxychloroquine, teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity with leflunomide, and myelosuppression with sulfasalazine.

teaching_points.claim: The American Academy of Ophthalmology and ACR guidelines recommend that the daily dose of hydroxychloroquine not exceed 5.0 mg/kg of actual body weight to minimize the cumulative risk of irreversible bull's-eye retinal maculopathy.

Baseline retinal evaluation is recommended within the first year of hydroxychloroquine initiation, followed by annual screening after 5 years of therapy using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and automated visual fields (10-2).

Leflunomide possesses an active metabolite (teriflunomide) with an elimination half-life of 2 to 4 weeks and extensive enterohepatic recirculation; in cases of acute hepatotoxicity or planned pregnancy, accelerated clearance using oral cholestyramine (8 g three times daily for 11 days) is mandatory.

Sulfasalazine requires baseline and routine complete blood count and liver enzyme monitoring every 2 to 4 weeks during the first 3 months of therapy due to risks of dose-dependent bone marrow suppression, hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency, and drug-induced hepatitis.

page.mentor_intro: Revascularization of left main coronary artery disease represents a pivotal clinical decision requiring multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation. Determining whether percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is optimal hinges on anatomical complexity, SYNTAX score, surgical risk, and comorbidities.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized EXCEL trial established that in patients with left main coronary disease and low-to-intermediate anatomical complexity (SYNTAX score <= 32), PCI with everolimus-eluting stents was noninferior to CABG for the composite of death, stroke, or MI at 3 and 5 years.

The NOBLE trial found that CABG was superior to PCI for major adverse cardiac or cerebrovascular events at 5 years in left main coronary disease, driven primarily by higher rates of repeat revascularization and non-procedural myocardial infarction in the PCI cohort.

In patients with high anatomical complexity (SYNTAX score >= 33) or complex multivessel disease with concurrent diabetes mellitus, CABG remains the preferred gold-standard revascularization strategy with superior long-term survival and freedom from recurrent ischemia.

When PCI is chosen for left main lesions, the routine use of intravascular imaging (IVUS or OCT) is strongly recommended to optimize stent sizing, ensure complete lesion coverage, and verify optimal stent expansion.

page.mentor_intro: Leishmaniasis encompasses a clinical spectrum ranging from self-limiting cutaneous lesions to life-threatening visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) caused by Leishmania donovani and L. infantum. Management requires prompt parasitological or serological diagnosis and species-directed antiparasitic chemotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: Visceral leishmaniasis is characterized by the clinical triad of prolonged irregular fever, progressive hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia, coupled with hypergammaglobulinemia and severe wasting.

The World Health Organization and IDSA guidelines recommend liposomal amphotericin B as the treatment of choice for visceral leishmaniasis, achieving cure rates exceeding 95% with significantly lower nephrotoxicity than conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate.

In visceral leishmaniasis with HIV co-infection, a randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated that combination therapy with liposomal amphotericin B plus oral miltefosine significantly increased 210-day cure rates and reduced relapses compared to liposomal amphotericin B monotherapy.

Definitive diagnosis requires visualization of Leishmania amastigotes on splenic, bone marrow, or lymph node aspirates, or rapid serological detection of antibodies against the recombinant rK39 antigen in immunocompetent hosts.

guidelinesKept: Leptomeningeal Metastasis from Solid Tumours: EANO-ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnosis, Treatment and Follow-Up

page.mentor_intro: Leptomeningeal metastasis represents diffuse tumor dissemination into the arachnoid membrane and cerebrospinal fluid, carrying a devastating prognosis. The 2023 EANO-ESMO guidelines emphasize multimodality management combining modern CNS-penetrant targeted therapies, focal radiation, and selective intrathecal pharmacotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 EANO-ESMO clinical practice guideline establishes that contrast-enhanced thin-slice whole neuroaxis MRI and CSF cytology are the gold standard diagnostic investigations for suspected leptomeningeal metastasis.

In patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer and leptomeningeal metastases, the third-generation EGFR-TKI osimertinib (including high-dose 160 mg daily regimens) demonstrates profound CNS penetration with objective CSF and neurological response rates.

Intrathecal chemotherapy (methotrexate, liposomal cytarabine, or pemetrexed) via an Ommaya reservoir is indicated primarily for diffuse linear cytologic disease without bulky nodular masses or CSF flow obstruction confirmed on radioisotope cisternography.

Focal radiotherapy is recommended to alleviate focal symptomatic cranial neuropathies, painful cauda equina nerve root compressions, or to relieve localized CSF flow obstructions prior to initiating intrathecal therapies.

guidelinesKept: Diagnosis and Management of AML in Adults: 2022 Recommendations from an International Expert Panel on Behalf of the ELN

page.mentor_intro: Acute leukemias represent clonal hematopoietic malignancies demanding emergency diagnostic cytogenetics, risk stratification, and prompt therapeutic induction. The 2022 European LeukemiaNet (ELN) recommendations establish molecular classifications and guide targeted therapies to overcome chemotherapy resistance.

teaching_points.claim: The 2022 European LeukemiaNet (ELN) recommendations categorize acute myeloid leukemia into favorable, intermediate, and adverse genetic risk categories based on cytogenetic fusions and defined somatic mutations (including TP53, NPM1, and FLT3-ITD).

In older adults or patients with AML ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy, the combination of the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent (azacitidine or decitabine) is standard of care, significantly improving complete remission and overall survival.

Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is an oncologic emergency requiring immediate initiation of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) upon clinical suspicion to avert fatal consumptive coagulopathy prior to cytogenetic confirmation of PML::RARA.

Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in first complete remission (CR1) is recommended for patients with adverse-risk and select intermediate-risk AML, whereas favorable-risk patients can be managed with consolidation chemotherapy.

guidelinesKept: Guidelines on the Use of Therapeutic Apheresis in Clinical Practice: Evidence-Based Approach from the American Society for Apheresis (ASFA 9th Special Issue)

page.mentor_intro: Leukostasis syndrome is a life-threatening medical emergency characterized by hyperleukocytosis (typically WBC > 100,000/uL in AML) resulting in microvascular sludging, tissue hypoxemia, and endothelial injury. Clinical priorities focus on rapid cytoreduction, aggressive hydration, tumor lysis prophylaxis, and immediate induction chemotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: Hyperleukocytosis is defined as a peripheral white blood cell count exceeding 100 x 10^9/L, with leukostasis syndrome presenting when circulating blasts obstruct microcirculation, predominantly manifesting as respiratory failure and neurological impairment.

The American Society for Apheresis (ASFA) categorizes therapeutic leukapheresis for hyperleukocytosis as Category III, reflecting that meta-analyses have shown it does not consistently reduce early 30-day mortality compared with chemotherapy alone.
Urgent medical cytoreduction with high-dose oral hydroxyurea (50 to 100 mg/kg/day) and immediate initiation of definitive induction chemotherapy should not be delayed to organize leukapheresis.

Packed red blood cell transfusions must be avoided or administered with extreme caution in un-cytoreduced patients with severe hyperleukocytosis because increasing blood hematocrit dramatically elevates whole-blood viscosity and precipitates fatal leukostatic infarctions.

topic: Lewy body dementia diagnosis and symptomatic therapy

guidelinesKept: Diagnosis and Management of Dementia with Lewy Bodies: Fourth Consensus Report of the DLB Consortium

page.mentor_intro: Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is the second most common neurodegenerative dementia in older adults. The 4th Consensus Report of the DLB Consortium establishes clinical criteria, validates indicative biomarkers, and outlines careful symptomatic pharmacotherapy emphasizing extreme sensitivity to neuroleptic agents.

teaching_points.claim: The 2017 Fourth Consensus Report of the DLB Consortium defines probable DLB by the presence of two or more core clinical features: fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention, recurrent formed visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder, and spontaneous parkinsonism.

Indicative biomarkers that confirm DLB in the presence of one core clinical feature include reduced dopamine transporter (DAT) uptake in the basal ganglia on SPECT/PET, reduced 123I-MIBG myocardial scintigraphy, and polysomnographic confirmation of REM sleep without atonia.

Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil and rivastigmine) are first-line pharmacotherapies in DLB, providing significant improvements in global cognitive function, apathy, and neuropsychiatric symptoms by addressing profound cortical cholinergic deficits.

First-generation and conventional antipsychotic medications are strictly contraindicated in DLB due to severe neuroleptic sensitivity reactions, which can trigger irreversible parkinsonism, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and increased mortality.

topic: Liberation from mechanical ventilation: weaning protocols

page.mentor_intro: Liberation from mechanical ventilation requires systematic daily assessment of extubation readiness to avoid complications of prolonged intubation or premature extubation. The ATS/CHEST guidelines recommend protocolized spontaneous breathing trials (SBTs) with inspiratory pressure augmentation over unassisted T-piece trials.

teaching_points.claim: The joint ATS/CHEST clinical practice guideline conditionally recommends conducting the initial spontaneous breathing trial with inspiratory pressure augmentation (pressure support 5 to 8 cm H2O) rather than unassisted breathing (T-piece or CPAP), which improves trial success and extubation rates.
Protocol-driven weaning led by respiratory therapists and nurses significantly reduces mechanical ventilation duration and ICU length of stay compared to physician-directed ad hoc weaning.

In patients at high risk for extubation failure (e.g., hypercapnic COPD, age > 65, heart failure), immediate post-extubation non-invasive ventilation (NIV) or high-flow nasal cannula prevents post-extubation respiratory failure and reintubation.

The rapid shallow breathing index (RSBI, f/Vt) below 105 breaths/min/L during spontaneous breathing remains a reliable physiological threshold to predict successful weaning, although cuff leak tests are necessary if laryngeal edema is suspected.

topic: Life-threatening arrhythmias in the ICU: VF, VT storm, advanced ACLS

page.mentor_intro: Electrical storm, defined as three or more distinct episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF) within 24 hours, is an acute medical emergency in the ICU. Management focuses on sympathetic overdrive suppression, electrolyte correction, targeted antiarrhythmic therapy, and emergency catheter ablation.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized OPTIC study demonstrated that the combination of a beta-blocker plus amiodarone is significantly superior to either beta-blockers alone or sotalol in suppressing recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and reducing ICD shocks.

The landmark VANISH trial established that in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy and refractory ventricular tachycardia despite antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation significantly reduces the composite outcome of death, VT storm, or ICD shocks compared to escalated antiarrhythmic therapy.

Emergency suppression of extreme sympathetic tone using deep sedation, endotracheal intubation, or percutaneous stellate ganglion block provides immediate stabilization in refractory electrical storm resistant to pharmacotherapy.

In recurrent ventricular fibrillation or polymorphic VT, urgent coronary angiography is mandatory to exclude acute myocardial ischemia, alongside aggressive repletion of serum potassium (>4.0 mEq/L) and magnesium (>2.0 mg/dL).

topic: Lipodystrophy syndromes: partial vs generalised, metabolic complications, leptin replacement

guidelinesKept: The Diagnosis and Management of Lipodystrophy Syndromes: A Multi-Society Practice Guideline

page.mentor_intro: Lipodystrophy syndromes are heterogeneous disorders characterized by selective loss of adipose tissue, leading to extreme ectopic lipid accumulation, severe insulin-resistant diabetes, and profound hypertriglyceridemia. Multi-society guidelines outline phenotypic categorization and recombinant human leptin (metreleptin) replacement.

teaching_points.claim: The multi-society practice guideline on lipodystrophy recommends recombinant human methionyl leptin (metreleptin) as an adjunct to diet for treating metabolic complications (severe hypertriglyceridemia and diabetes) in patients with generalized lipodystrophy.

Congenital generalized lipodystrophy (Berardinelli-Seip syndrome) presents at birth with near-total absence of subcutaneous adipose tissue, whereas familial partial lipodystrophy (Dunnigan variety, LMNA mutations) typically manifests at puberty with loss of extremity and trunk fat but facial and neck sparing.

Severe hypoleptinemia secondary to adipose absence impairs central satiety signaling, driving severe hyperphagia, marked hepatic steatosis progressing to cirrhosis, and extreme hypertriglyceridemia precipitating recurrent acute pancreatitis.

In partial lipodystrophy, metreleptin therapy is considered primarily for selected patients with proven severe hypoleptinemia and severe refractory metabolic disease (HbA1c > 8% or triglycerides > 500 mg/dL despite maximized standard pharmacotherapy).

guidelinesKept: Haemodialysis for Lithium Poisoning: Translating EXTRIP Recommendations into Practical Guidelines

page.mentor_intro: Lithium remains the gold standard mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder but has a narrow therapeutic index (0.6 to 1.0 mmol/L) and exclusive renal elimination. Prevention and management of toxicity rely on structured serum surveillance, recognition of drug interactions, and timely extracorporeal clearance.

teaching_points.claim: NICE guidelines recommend checking 12-hour trough serum lithium levels every 3 to 6 months in stable patients, alongside mandatory renal function (creatinine, eGFR), calcium, and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) every 6 months.

The EXTRIP workgroup guidelines recommend hemodialysis for severe lithium poisoning when serum concentration exceeds 4.0 mmol/L in acute toxicity, or exceeds 2.5 mmol/L in chronic toxicity with severe neurological signs or renal impairment.

Co-administration of thiazide diuretics, NSAIDs, or ACE inhibitors/ARBs impairs renal lithium clearance by promoting compensatory proximal tubular sodium and lithium reabsorption, precipitating acute-on-chronic toxicity.

Chronic lithium nephrotoxicity typically manifests as nephrogenic diabetes insipidus due to down-regulation of aquaporin-2 water channels in the renal collecting duct, leading to polyuria, polydipsia, and volume depletion.

guidelinesKept: Baveno VII - Renewing Consensus in Portal Hypertension: Report of the Baveno VII Consensus Workshop

page.mentor_intro: Cirrhosis represents end-stage hepatic fibrosis complicated by portal hypertension and liver synthetic failure. The Baveno VII consensus guidelines have transformed clinical management through validated non-invasive testing for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and risk-stratified variceal screening.

teaching_points.claim: The Baveno VII consensus establishes that clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH, HVPG >= 10 mmHg) can be reliably ruled out non-invasively if liver stiffness measurement is < 15 kPa and platelet count is > 150,000/uL, allowing patients to safely avoid screening endoscopy.

Non-selective beta-blockers, specifically carvedilol (starting at 6.25 mg daily), are the preferred first-line pharmacological therapy to reduce portal pressure and prevent first hepatic decompensation in patients with CSPH.

A liver stiffness measurement by transient elastography > 25 kPa confirms the presence of clinically significant portal hypertension non-invasively without requiring invasive hepatic venous pressure gradient measurement.

In patients with cirrhosis and ascites, diagnostic paracentesis is mandatory upon hospital admission to rule out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (defined as ascitic fluid neutrophil count >= 250 cells/mm3).

guidelinesKept: Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnosis, Treatment and Follow-Up

page.mentor_intro: Colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) represent the primary determinant of survival in stage IV colorectal cancer. Multidisciplinary tumor board evaluation is paramount to determine resectability, future liver remnant (FLR) volume, and the sequencing of conversion chemotherapy versus upfront surgical resection.

teaching_points.claim: The ESMO clinical practice guidelines mandate that all patients with colorectal liver metastases be evaluated by a multidisciplinary team including hepatobiliary surgeons to assess technical resectability based on achieving an R0 resection with adequate future liver remnant (>20-30%).

In patients with initially unresectable, liver-limited metastases, intensive conversion systemic chemotherapy (FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, or FOLFOXIRI) combined with a targeted biologic based on RAS/BRAF mutation status and primary tumor sidedness achieves secondary resectability in 15% to 30% of cases.
Surgical resection of isolated colorectal liver metastases provides curative potential, achieving 5-year overall survival rates of 40% to 55% in contemporary surgical series.

For marginal future liver remnants, preoperative portal vein embolization (PVE) or associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) can induce contralateral liver hypertrophy to permit safe subsequent resection.

guidelinesKept: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Liver Transplantation

page.mentor_intro: Timely referral for liver transplantation is essential to optimize survival in end-stage liver disease and acute liver failure. Clinical guidelines emphasize that referral should occur at the earliest sign of hepatic decompensation or when the MELD-Na score reaches 15, rather than waiting for critical illness.

teaching_points.claim: The AASLD and AST practice guidelines recommend referring patients with cirrhosis for liver transplantation evaluation when the MELD-Na score is >= 15 or upon the appearance of any major clinical decompensation (ascites, encephalopathy, variceal hemorrhage).
MELD-Na incorporates serum sodium alongside bilirubin, creatinine, and INR, significantly improving 90-day waitlist mortality prediction in patients with hyponatremia and portal hypertension.

Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma meeting Milan criteria (single tumor <= 5 cm or up to 3 tumors each <= 3 cm without vascular invasion) qualify for standardized MELD exception points to balance their drop-out risk.

Acute liver failure requires immediate transfer to a transplant center prior to advanced encephalopathy; King's College Criteria remain an established prognostic tool to predict mortality without emergent transplantation.

topic: Living kidney donor evaluation and long-term risk

guidelinesKept: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline on the Evaluation and Care of Living Kidney Donors

page.mentor_intro: Living kidney donor evaluation ensures donor safety, voluntary informed consent, and recipient compatibility. The KDIGO guidelines framework replaces rigid single-parameter exclusions with an individualized quantitative lifetime risk assessment of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

teaching_points.claim: The KDIGO clinical practice guideline on living kidney donor evaluation incorporates quantitative 15-year and projected lifetime ESKD risk tools, recommending that acceptable risk thresholds be transparently communicated to donor candidates.

Direct measurement of glomerular filtration rate (using inulin, iohexol, or 24-hour creatinine clearance) is recommended when estimated GFR is borderline, with an absolute GFR >= 90 mL/min/1.73 m2 generally considered acceptable for donation.

Persistent overt proteinuria (albuminuria > 30 mg/24 hours or protein > 150 mg/24 hours) or untreated hypertension with target-organ damage represents an unacceptable long-term renal risk, precluding living donation.

Longitudinal cohort studies establish that while living kidney donors face a slightly higher relative risk of ESKD compared to exceptionally healthy non-donors, their absolute lifetime risk remains very low (<1% in most white donors).

topic: Long COVID and post-infectious syndromes: fatigue, dysautonomia, mechanism, management

guidelinesKept: Management of the Long-Term Effects of COVID-19: Summary of NICE Guideline

page.mentor_intro: Post-COVID-19 syndrome encompasses persistent multisystem symptoms continuing beyond 12 weeks post-infection. The NICE guideline outlines holistic multidisciplinary assessment, screening for postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and post-exertional malaise, and symptom-titrated pacing rehabilitation.

teaching_points.claim: NICE guideline NG188 defines post-COVID-19 syndrome as signs and symptoms that develop during or after an infection consistent with COVID-19, continue for more than 12 weeks, and are not explained by an alternative diagnosis.

Dysautonomia, specifically Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), is a recognized complication of Long COVID characterized by a sustained heart rate increase >= 30 bpm within 10 minutes of standing without orthostatic hypotension.

Post-exertional malaise (PEM), defined as a disproportionate worsening of symptoms following minimal physical or cognitive exertion, must be screened for prior to initiating any exercise program to prevent debilitating post-exertional crashes.

Management centers on symptom-titrated energy pacing, autonomic conditioning (increased fluid/sodium intake and compression garments for orthostatic intolerance), and avoiding fixed graded exercise therapy when PEM is present.

topic: long-term adverse effects of proton pump inhibitors
cluster: long term adverse effects of proton pump inhibitors

page.mentor_intro: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are among the most widely prescribed medications globally. While highly effective for acid-peptic disorders, accumulating clinical trial data and guidelines urge regular reassessment and deprescribing to avoid long-term adverse renal, bone, and infectious complications.

teaching_points.claim: A post-hoc analysis of the randomized COMPASS trial (over 17,500 patients) published in JASN demonstrated that long-term pantoprazole therapy was associated with a statistically significant, faster annual decline in estimated GFR compared to placebo.

Chronic PPI therapy induces gastric hypochlorhydria, which impairs dietary protein-bound vitamin B12 cleavage, reduces non-heme iron and magnesium absorption, and increases the risk of hypomagnesemic hypocalcemia.

Large observational studies link long-term PPI therapy with an increased risk of Clostridioides difficile infection, community-acquired pneumonia, and microscopic colitis through disruption of the gut microbiome and loss of the protective gastric acid barrier.

Clinical practice guidelines recommend periodic re-evaluation of long-term PPI indications, advising dose reduction or trial deprescribing for uncomplicated GERD or non-ulcer dyspepsia while maintaining therapy for severe erosive esophagitis or Barrett's esophagus.

guidelinesKept: Home Oxygen Therapy for Adults with Chronic Lung Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline

page.mentor_intro: Long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) improves survival in chronic lung disease patients with severe resting hypoxemia. The landmark NOTT and MRC trials established mortality reduction for severe hypoxemia, while the modern LOTT trial confirmed an absence of benefit in moderate desaturation.

teaching_points.claim: The landmark NOTT and MRC trials established that long-term continuous oxygen therapy (>= 15 to 18 hours/day) significantly reduces mortality in patients with stable COPD and severe resting hypoxemia (PaO2 <= 55 mmHg or SaO2 <= 88%).

The randomized LOTT trial established that supplemental oxygen does not improve time to death or first hospitalization, nor does it improve quality of life, in patients with stable COPD and only moderate resting (SpO2 89% to 93%) or exercise desaturation.

The 2020 American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline strongly recommends prescribing continuous LTOT (at least 15 hours/day) for adults with COPD and severe resting chronic hypoxemia, while recommending against routine LTOT in moderate desaturation.

In patients with PaO2 between 56 and 59 mmHg (SaO2 89%), LTOT is indicated if there is objective evidence of cor pulmonale, peripheral dependent edema from right heart failure, or secondary polycythemia (hematocrit > 55%).

page.mentor_intro: Epidemiological cohorts following patients for up to three years provide clarity on the long-term prognosis of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Mortality and multiorgan risk trajectories differ markedly depending on whether the index infection required hospitalization.

teaching_points.claim: A landmark 2-year cohort study in Nature Medicine demonstrated that in non-hospitalized individuals with COVID-19, the excess risk of death and hospitalization resolved after the first year, whereas in hospitalized individuals, mortality risk remained significantly elevated through 2 years.

A 3-year follow-up study of 135,000 individuals confirmed that while new incident sequelae decline over time, substantial cumulative disability and health loss persist at 3 years, particularly in post-exertional fatigue, dysautonomia, and neurocognitive impairment.
Prior vaccination against COVID-19 significantly attenuates the long-term risk of developing persistent post-acute sequelae and multiorgan complications compared to unvaccinated controls.

Hospitalization during acute infection serves as the primary prognostic determinant, with hospitalized cohorts experiencing sustained multiorgan vulnerability across cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, and neurological domains through 36 months.

page.mentor_intro: Low back pain (LBP) is the leading global cause of disability. Clinical practice guidelines from the American College of Physicians (ACP) emphasize non-pharmacological interventions as first-line therapy, advise against routine spinal imaging, and recommend avoiding acetaminophen following negative landmark trial evidence.

teaching_points.claim: The American College of Physicians clinical guideline strongly recommends that initial management of acute, subacute, and chronic low back pain prioritize non-pharmacological therapy (heat, spinal manipulation, massage, acupuncture, and physical therapy).

The randomized PACE trial published in The Lancet established that regular or as-needed paracetamol (acetaminophen) does not speed recovery time, reduce pain, or reduce disability compared to placebo in acute low back pain.

Routine lumbar spine imaging (X-ray, CT, or MRI) is strongly discouraged in the absence of clinical red flags (fever, unexplained weight loss, history of cancer, progressive neurologic deficit, or cauda equina signs) as imaging does not improve outcomes and increases unnecessary interventions.

When pharmacotherapy is necessary for acute low back pain, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or short-term skeletal muscle relaxants are recommended over acetaminophen, while opioids and systemic steroids should be avoided.

page.mentor_intro: Sciatica (lumbosacral radicular pain) typically arises from disc herniation compressing a nerve root. The NICE NG59 guidelines recommend differentiating radicular pain from non-specific low back pain, utilizing epidural local anesthetic and corticosteroid injections for acute severe pain, and referring for surgical microdiscectomy when disabling symptoms persist.

teaching_points.claim: The NICE NG59 guidelines recommend considering epidural injections of local anesthetic and corticosteroid for patients with acute, severe sciatica to provide short- to medium-term radicular pain relief.

The Spine Patient Outcomes Research Trial (SPORT) demonstrated that lumbar discectomy for herniated intervertebral disc achieves significantly faster pain relief and functional recovery compared to non-operative care, though long-term outcomes at 4 to 8 years show convergence.

NICE explicitly recommends that patient factors such as body mass index (BMI), smoking status, or psychological distress should not be used to deny or delay surgical referral for persistent or disabling sciatica.

Emergent MRI and immediate surgical decompression within 48 hours are mandatory for suspected cauda equina syndrome, clinically signaled by saddle anesthesia, progressive bilateral motor weakness, and new bladder or bowel dysfunction.

guidelinesKept: Management of Patients With Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding: An Updated ACG Guideline

page.mentor_intro: Acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB) ranges from self-limiting hematochezia to life-threatening hemorrhage. The 2023 ACG guidelines recommend objective risk stratification with the Oakland score to identify low-risk outpatients, restrictive blood transfusion thresholds, and early diagnostic CT angiography or colonoscopy in high-risk hemodynamic instability.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 ACG clinical guideline on lower GI bleeding recommends using the validated Oakland score (threshold <= 8 points) to safely identify low-risk patients who can be discharged from the emergency department for outpatient investigation.

A restrictive packed red blood cell transfusion strategy targeting a hemoglobin threshold of 7 g/dL (target 7 to 9 g/dL) is recommended for hemodynamically stable patients, improving survival and reducing rebleeding compared to liberal transfusion (threshold 9 g/dL).

In patients presenting with severe, ongoing hematochezia and hemodynamic instability, an upper endoscopy should be performed if an upper GI source is suspected, or immediate CT angiography should be utilized to localize active bleeding prior to catheter angiography and embolization.

For hospitalized patients requiring inpatient colonoscopy, the procedure should be performed following adequate oral colon lavage; early urgent colonoscopy (<24 hours) has not been shown to reduce rebleeding or mortality compared to elective next-day colonoscopy.

page.mentor_intro: Male lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) require objective symptom scoring and risk stratification for disease progression. Landmark trials establish that combining an alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist with a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor (5-ARI) prevents acute urinary retention and surgical intervention in enlarged prostates.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized MTOPS trial (over 3,000 men followed for 4.5 years) demonstrated that combination therapy with doxazosin plus finasteride reduced the risk of overall clinical progression of BPH by 66%, significantly outperforming either monotherapy.

The 4-year CombAT trial confirmed that dutasteride plus tamsulosin combination therapy significantly reduced the relative risk of acute urinary retention or BPH-related surgery by 65.8% compared to tamsulosin monotherapy in men with prostate volume >= 30 mL.

EAU and AUA guidelines recommend 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride) specifically for men with moderate-to-severe LUTS and documented prostate enlargement (volume > 30-40 mL or PSA > 1.5 ng/mL) to modify natural disease progression.

Alpha-blockers provide rapid symptomatic relief within 48 to 72 hours by reducing prostatic smooth muscle tone, whereas 5-ARIs require 6 to 12 months to induce epithelial atrophy and reduce prostate volume by approximately 20% to 25%.

page.mentor_intro: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) features non-hydrostatic pulmonary edema and severe hypoxemia. The landmark ARMA trial by the ARDS Network established that lung-protective ventilation using low tidal volumes and restricted plateau pressures significantly reduces hospital mortality.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized ARDSNet ARMA trial established that mechanical ventilation with a low tidal volume target of 6 mL/kg of predicted body weight significantly reduced mortality from 39.8% to 31.0% (P=0.007) compared to traditional 12 mL/kg ventilation.

Lung-protective ventilation mandates maintaining end-inspiratory plateau pressure at or below 30 cm H2O to prevent alveolar overdistension and ventilator-induced lung injury (volutrauma and barotrauma).

Tidal volume calculations in ARDS must be strictly based on predicted (ideal) body weight determined by height and sex, rather than actual measured body weight, to prevent occult severe volutrauma in obese individuals.

Permissive hypercapnia with mild respiratory acidosis (pH >= 7.20 to 7.25) is an accepted physiological trade-off when implementing 6 mL/kg ventilation to limit alveolar stretch in severely non-compliant lungs.

page.mentor_intro: Lumbar spinal stenosis results from degenerative narrowing of the spinal canal causing neurogenic claudication. The landmark SPORT trial demonstrated that surgical decompression provides substantial and durable pain and functional improvements over non-operative care in patients with persistent disabling symptoms.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized and observational SPORT trial cohorts demonstrated that patients with symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis treated surgically with decompressive laminectomy achieved significantly greater improvements in bodily pain and physical function through 2 to 4 years compared to non-operative management.

Neurogenic claudication is the classic clinical hallmark of lumbar stenosis, characterized by bilateral leg pain, paresthesias, and cramping exacerbated by walking and lumbar extension, and relieved by sitting or forward lumbar flexion (shopping cart sign).

Vascular claudication is differentiated clinically from neurogenic claudication by relief with standing still without flexion, preserved pedal pulses in neurogenic claudication, and pain brought on consistently by fixed distances regardless of posture.

Decompressive laminectomy alone is the surgical standard for stenosis without instability, whereas adjunctive spinal fusion is indicated only when concurrent spondylolisthesis or frank spinal instability is documented.

page.mentor_intro: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Population-level screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces mortality, while comprehensive molecular profiling for actionable oncogenic driver mutations dictates first-line systemic therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) demonstrated a 20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality with annual low-dose CT screening compared to chest radiography in high-risk smokers.
The European NELSON trial confirmed a 24% to 26% reduction in lung cancer mortality at 10 years using volumetric low-dose CT nodule screening with low referral rates.

In advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), broad-panel next-generation sequencing (NGS) is mandatory to identify actionable alterations including EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, RET, MET exon 14 skipping, and KRAS G12C prior to initiating immunotherapy.

First-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC and alectinib in ALK-rearranged NSCLC significantly prolong progression-free and overall survival while providing superior central nervous system protection compared to early-generation TKIs.

page.mentor_intro: Lung cancer screening guidelines balance early detection of resectable malignancies against the harms of false positives, incidental findings, and radiation exposure. The 2021 USPSTF update expanded eligibility by lowering both the age threshold and the cumulative pack-year requirement.

teaching_points.claim: The 2021 USPSTF recommendation statement expanded lung cancer screening eligibility to adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years.

Lowering the eligibility threshold to age 50 and 20 pack-years significantly increased screening sensitivity and reduced racial disparities in screening access, particularly for African American and female smokers who develop lung cancer at lower pack-years.
Screening should be discontinued once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a substantial health condition that limits life expectancy or the ability to undergo curative lung resection.

Shared decision-making is a mandatory guideline component prior to screening, emphasizing the benefits of early mortality reduction, smoking cessation counseling, and the potential risks of nodule workups and overdiagnosis.

page.mentor_intro: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) utilizes modern helical CT techniques to minimize radiation while identifying early-stage curable lung cancers. teaching_points.claim: The landmark NELSON trial demonstrated that volume-based CT screening with semi-automated nodule volume calculation and volume doubling time (VDT) yields an exceptionally low referral rate (2.1%) while reducing 10-year lung cancer mortality by 24% in men.

The Lung-RADS classification categorizes nodules from 1 (negative) to 4X (very high suspicion), with category 3 (probably benign) managed with 6-month repeat LDCT and category 4 managed with diagnostic workup or PET/CT.
Radiation exposure from a modern low-dose chest CT is approximately 1.0 to 1.5 mSv, compared to 7 to 8 mSv for a standard diagnostic chest CT, making annual serial surveillance safe.

Subsolid (part-solid and pure ground-glass) nodules detected on LDCT exhibit indolent biology; guidelines mandate conservative observation with serial low-dose CT to document persistent growth or appearance of a solid component prior to resection.

page.mentor_intro: Lung transplantation offers survival and functional improvement for selected patients with end-stage respiratory failure refractory to medical therapy. The 2021 ISHLT consensus guidelines provide clear criteria differentiating the optimal timing for initial transplant referral from definitive waitlist listing.

teaching_points.claim: The 2021 ISHLT consensus document on candidate selection recommends referring patients with chronic lung disease for transplant evaluation when their estimated 2- to 3-year mortality exceeds 50%, or when oxygen dependence and severe functional impairment manifest.

In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), immediate referral for lung transplantation at the time of initial clinical diagnosis is strongly recommended, regardless of baseline FVC, due to the unpredictable and rapid trajectory of disease progression.

Absolute contraindications to lung transplantation under ISHLT guidelines include active malignancy within 2 years, severe uncorrectable multi-organ dysfunction (cardiac, renal, hepatic), active non-adherence, and active substance use or smoking within 6 months.
In COPD, referral is recommended for BODE index >= 5, FEV1 < 25% predicted, or refractory hypercapnic exacerbations, while listing is indicated for BODE index >= 7.

page.mentor_intro: Lupus nephritis represents a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus that leads to end-stage kidney disease if untreated. The KDIGO 2024 guidelines endorse early triple/multitarget therapy combining glucocorticoids and antimetabolites with belimumab or calcineurin inhibitors (voclosporin).

teaching_points.claim: The KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guidelines recommend initial treatment of active proliferative lupus nephritis (Class III/IV) with reduced-dose glucocorticoids plus mycophenolic acid analogs (or low-dose IV cyclophosphamide), with upfront addition of belimumab or voclosporin for triple therapy.

The landmark BLISS-LN phase 3 trial demonstrated that adding intravenous belimumab to standard of care significantly increased primary efficacy renal response at week 104 (43% vs 32%, P=0.03) and significantly reduced renal flare rates.

The AURORA 1 trial established that adding the novel calcineurin inhibitor voclosporin to mycophenolate mofetil and low-dose oral steroids significantly doubled complete renal response rates at 52 weeks (41% vs 23%, P<0.0001) without increasing nephrotoxicity.

All patients with lupus nephritis should receive background hydroxychloroquine (unless strictly contraindicated) at a target dose not exceeding 5.0 mg/kg actual body weight to reduce renal flares and improve survival.

topic: Lupus nephritis induction and maintenance therapy

guidelinesKept: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Lupus Nephritis

page.mentor_intro: Induction and maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis aims to achieve rapid remission while preserving nephron mass and minimizing corticosteroid toxicity. Seminal trials (ALMS and MAINTAIN) established mycophenolate mofetil as equal or superior to cyclophosphamide for induction and maintenance.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized ALMS trial demonstrated that mycophenolate mofetil (target 3 g/day) is noninferior to monthly intravenous cyclophosphamide for induction of remission in active lupus nephritis, showing superior efficacy in African American and Hispanic populations.

In the maintenance phase of the ALMS trial, mycophenolate mofetil was significantly superior to azathioprine in preventing renal relapse (HR 0.44, P=0.003) and treatment failure in patients who responded to induction.

The MAINTAIN Nephritis trial confirmed low-dose intravenous cyclophosphamide (Euro-Lupus regimen: 500 mg every 2 weeks for 6 doses) is equally effective as high-dose monthly NIH cyclophosphamide with significantly lower rates of severe infection and premature ovarian failure.
Maintenance immunosuppressive therapy for lupus nephritis must be continued for a minimum of 36 to 48 months following complete renal response before considering gradual taper.

topic: Lupus nephritis: ISN/RPS classification, biopsy indications, induction therapy

guidelinesKept: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Lupus Nephritis

page.mentor_intro: The ISN/RPS classification system provides a standardized histological framework for lupus nephritis. Renal biopsy is mandatory in SLE patients with unexplained proteinuria, active urinary sediment, or declining renal function to differentiate proliferative disease requiring intensive immunosuppression from non-proliferative forms.

teaching_points.claim: The ISN/RPS histological classification categorizes lupus nephritis into six classes: I (minimal mesangial), II (mesangial proliferative), III (focal proliferative, <50% glomeruli), IV (diffuse proliferative, >=50% glomeruli), V (membranous), and VI (advanced sclerosing).

Renal biopsy is indicated in SLE whenever there is persistent proteinuria >= 0.5 g/24 hours (or spot UPCR >= 0.5 mg/mg), active urinary sediment (>5 RBCs/HPF or cellular casts), or an unexplained rise in serum creatinine.

Class III and IV proliferative lesions carry the highest risk of progression to end-stage renal disease and mandate immediate aggressive immunosuppressive induction therapy with corticosteroids plus MMF or cyclophosphamide.

Renal biopsy reporting must include the NIH Activity and Chronicity Indices, which evaluate reversible inflammatory lesions (cellular crescents, endocapillary proliferation, necrosis) versus irreversible fibrosis (glomerulosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis).

topic: Lupus Pneumonitis and Shrinking Lung Syndrome
cluster: lupus pneumonitis and shrinking lung syndrome

page.mentor_intro: Pulmonary complications of systemic lupus erythematosus range from acute life-threatening lupus pneumonitis to insidious shrinking lung syndrome (SLS). Shrinking lung syndrome is characterized by progressive dyspnea, pleuritic pain, elevated diaphragms, and restrictive physiology in the absence of parenchymal lung disease.

teaching_points.claim: Shrinking lung syndrome is a rare manifestation of SLE characterized by exertional dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, elevated hemidiaphragms on imaging, and reduced lung volumes without interstitial fibrosis or pulmonary vascular obstruction.

Pulmonary function testing in shrinking lung syndrome demonstrates a pure extrapulmonary restrictive defect with proportional reductions in FVC, FEV1, and TLC, accompanied by reduced maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressures (MIP/MEP) reflecting diaphragmatic weakness.

Acute lupus pneumonitis presents acutely with fever, cough, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxemia, and diffuse alveolar infiltrates on CT, requiring exclusion of opportunistic infection and high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

Management of shrinking lung syndrome combines moderate-to-high dose corticosteroids with immunosuppressive agents (mycophenolate mofetil, azathioprine, or rituximab), with beta-agonists or theophylline occasionally used to enhance diaphragmatic contractility.

guidelinesKept: Clinical Practice Guidelines by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), American Academy of Neurology (AAN), and American College of Rheumatology (ACR): 2020 Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Lyme Disease

page.mentor_intro: Lyme arthritis is a late-stage manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection, typically presenting as monoarticular or oligoarticular inflammatory arthritis of large joints, predominantly the knee. Joint IDSA/AAN/ACR guidelines establish a 28-day oral antibiotic regimen as first-line therapy, reserving IV ceftriaxone for persistent non-responsive synovitis.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 joint IDSA/AAN/ACR guidelines recommend an initial 28-day course of oral antibiotics (doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily, or cefuroxime axetil 500 mg twice daily) as first-line therapy for Lyme arthritis.

If joint swelling and inflammation persist after an initial 28-day oral course, guidelines recommend either a second 28-day course of oral antibiotics or a 14- to 28-day course of intravenous ceftriaxone (2 g once daily).

Post-antibiotic (antibiotic-refractory) Lyme arthritis is defined as persistent joint inflammation despite appropriate oral and IV antibiotic therapy; further antibiotic courses are not recommended and treatment should transition to anti-inflammatory therapies (NSAIDs, DMARDs, or intra-articular corticosteroids).

Diagnostic confirmation of Lyme arthritis requires positive two-tier serology (or modified two-tier serology), with synovial fluid PCR for Borrelia burgdorferi DNA demonstrating high sensitivity prior to antibiotic exposure.

topic: Lyme disease: Borrelia, tick bite, erythema migrans, disseminated disease, doxycycline

guidelinesKept: Clinical Practice Guidelines by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), American Academy of Neurology (AAN), and American College of Rheumatology (ACR): 2020 Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Lyme Disease

page.mentor_intro: Lyme disease is a multisystem vector-borne zoonosis transmitted by Ixodes scapularis and I. pacificus ticks infected with Borrelia burgdorferi. Clinical presentation dictates management: erythema migrans warrants immediate clinical diagnosis and treatment without serological delay, whereas post-tick bite prophylaxis requires strict eligibility criteria.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 IDSA/AAN/ACR guidelines recommend a single prophylactic dose of oral doxycycline (200 mg) only when an attached blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis) was removed after >= 36 hours of attachment in a highly endemic area, within 72 hours of tick removal.

The presence of a classic expanding erythema migrans rash (>= 5 cm) following potential tick exposure in an endemic area is diagnostic of early Lyme disease; serological testing is insensitive in early localized infection (<50%) and should not be performed.

Oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily for 10 to 14 days) is the first-line treatment for early localized Lyme disease and early disseminated disease without severe carditis or central nervous system involvement.

In early disseminated Lyme disease presenting as isolated cranial nerve palsy (e.g. unilateral or bilateral Bell's palsy), oral doxycycline is equally effective as intravenous ceftriaxone in the absence of objective meningitis signs.

guidelinesKept: Clinical Practice Guidelines by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), American Academy of Neurology (AAN), and American College of Rheumatology (ACR): 2020 Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Lyme Disease

page.mentor_intro: Accurate diagnosis of Lyme disease relies on stage-dependent clinical evaluation and validated two-tier laboratory algorithms. The CDC and FDA have approved modified two-tier testing (MTTT) utilizing sequential enzyme immunoassays (EIAs) including the C6 peptide, improving sensitivity in early disease without sacrificing specificity.

teaching_points.claim: The CDC and IDSA endorse modified two-tier testing (MTTT) protocols using two sequential enzyme immunoassays (EIAs) or chemiluminescent immunoassays (such as C6 peptide EIA) as an acceptable alternative to traditional Western blot second-tier testing.

Standard two-tier testing requires an initial sensitive EIA; if positive or equivocal, it is reflexed to a Western blot, requiring >= 2 of 3 bands on IgM Western blot (24, 39, 41 kDa) within the first 30 days of infection, or >= 5 of 10 bands on IgG Western blot after 30 days.
An isolated positive IgM Western blot in a patient with symptoms lasting more than 30 days represents a false-positive result and should not be used to support a diagnosis of chronic Lyme disease.

Lyme serology (IgG antibodies) commonly remains positive for years or decades following successful curative treatment and does not reflect persistent active infection or require repeated antibiotic therapy.

page.mentor_intro: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, progressive, multi-system neoplastic disease primarily affecting women of childbearing age, characterized by cystic lung destruction, angiomyolipomas, and chylous effusions due to TSC1/TSC2 mutations. The landmark MILES trial established sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor) as the first disease-modifying therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized, double-blind MILES trial demonstrated that the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus stabilizes lung function decline (FEV1), reduces serum VEGF-D levels, and improves functional capacity and quality of life in patients with moderate-to-severe LAM.

In the MILES trial, the beneficial effects of sirolimus were suppressive rather than curative; upon cessation of sirolimus therapy, lung function decline resumed at a rate parallel to the placebo group, demonstrating the necessity of lifelong maintenance.

The ATS/JRS clinical practice guidelines recommend sirolimus as first-line therapy for patients with LAM who have abnormal or declining lung function (FEV1 < 70% predicted or annual decline >= 90 mL/year), symptomatic chylous effusions, or renal angiomyolipomas > 4 cm.

Serum vascular endothelial growth factor-D (VEGF-D) elevation (>= 800 pg/mL) in a patient with characteristic high-resolution chest CT cystic changes confirms the diagnosis of LAM without requiring lung biopsy.

page.mentor_intro: Pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis (PLC) represents diffuse hematogenous or retrograde lymphatic dissemination of malignant cells throughout the pulmonary interstitium. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) provides pathognomonic diagnostic accuracy, frequently obviating the need for invasive surgical lung biopsy in frail cancer patients.

teaching_points.claim: High-resolution CT (HRCT) characteristically demonstrates irregular, nodular thickening of the interlobular septa and bronchovascular interstitium, preserving normal lobular architecture without architectural distortion.
Primary adenocarcinomas of the lung, breast, stomach, colon, pancreas, and prostate account for more than 80% of secondary pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis cases.

The clinical presentation is marked by severe progressive exertional dyspnea and non-productive cough that are often profoundly out of proportion to initial subtle plain chest radiographic abnormalities.

Palliative management focuses on treating the underlying primary malignancy with systemic therapy, alongside adjunctive oral or intravenous corticosteroids to reduce peritumoral interstitial edema and alleviate breathlessness.

page.mentor_intro: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The landmark phase 3 POLARIX trial modified the decades-old standard-of-care R-CHOP regimen by demonstrating that Pola-R-CHP significantly improves progression-free survival in previously untreated intermediate- and high-risk patients.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized phase 3 POLARIX trial demonstrated that replacing vincristine with the anti-CD79b antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin (Pola-R-CHP) significantly prolonged progression-free survival (HR 0.73, P=0.02) compared to standard R-CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL.

The International Prognostic Index (IPI score, based on age > 60, elevated LDH, ECOG >= 2, stage III/IV, and >1 extranodal site) risk-stratifies DLBCL patients to predict long-term complete response and survival.

Definitive diagnosis requires excisional lymph node biopsy rather than fine-needle aspiration to accurately assess nodal architecture, cell-of-origin (germinal center B-cell vs activated B-cell), and evaluate MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements (double-hit lymphoma).

In patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL within 12 months of first-line chemoimmunotherapy, CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is preferred over salvage chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation.

guidelinesKept: 2016 Classification Criteria for Macrophage Activation Syndrome Complicating Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology/Paediatric Rheumatology International Trials Organisation Collaborative Initiative

page.mentor_intro: Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS) is a life-threatening form of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) occurring in systemic autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases, most notably systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) and adult-onset Still's disease. The 2016 EULAR/ACR criteria emphasize extreme hyperferritinemia and targeted IL-1 blockade.

teaching_points.claim: The 2016 EULAR/ACR classification criteria establish that diagnosing MAS in febrile systemic JIA requires serum ferritin > 684 ng/mL plus at least two of: platelets <= 181 x 10^9/L, AST > 48 U/L, triglycerides > 156 mg/dL, or fibrinogen <= 360 mg/dL.

A falling erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) in the setting of persistent high fever and rising serum ferritin is a classic diagnostic red flag for MAS, reflecting acute consumptive hypofibrinogenemia.
High-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (30 mg/kg/day, maximum 1 g/day for 3 consecutive days) is first-line induction therapy for acute macrophage activation syndrome.
Targeted interleukin-1 blockade with recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra (often at high doses, 4 to 10 mg/kg/day) provides rapid disease control in steroid-refractory or severe MAS.

page.mentor_intro: Major depressive disorder (MDD) pharmacotherapy balances symptom reduction against medication tolerability. The landmark NIMH-sponsored STAR*D trial provided real-world evidence on sequential antidepressant steps, demonstrating that one-third of patients remit on first-line SSRI monotherapy and that remission rates decline with successive failed steps.

teaching_points.claim: The benchmark STAR*D trial demonstrated that initial first-line monotherapy with the SSRI citalopram achieved clinical symptom remission in only 28% to 33% of outpatients with major depressive disorder using measurement-based care.

In STAR*D, over 40% of patients who ultimately achieved remission required at least 8 to 12 weeks of optimized antidepressant dose titration, emphasizing adequate treatment duration before declaring treatment failure.

With each successive failed treatment step in STAR*D (switching class vs augmenting with bupropion, buspirone, or lithium), the acute remission rate progressively dropped (from ~30% in Level 1 to <15% in Level 4), while relapse rates rose.

Measurement-based care using standardized rating scales (PHQ-9, QIDS-SR) at each clinical visit is strongly recommended to identify residual depressive symptoms, which represent the strongest predictor of rapid relapse.

page.mentor_intro: Malaria remains a leading cause of global parasitic morbidity and mortality. Landmark multicenter trials (SEAQUAMAT and AQUAMAT) revolutionized management by proving that parenteral artesunate significantly reduces mortality compared to intravenous quinine in severe falciparum malaria.

teaching_points.claim: The randomized AQUAMAT trial (over 5,400 African children) established that parenteral artesunate reduced mortality by 22.5% (8.5% vs 10.9%, P=0.002) compared to intravenous quinine for severe falciparum malaria.

The SEAQUAMAT trial in Asian adults demonstrated a 34.7% relative reduction in mortality with artesunate compared to quinine (15% vs 22%, P=0.0002), establishing intravenous artesunate as the global standard of care.

Artesunate possesses a superior safety profile compared to quinine, which frequently triggers profound hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, cardiac dysrhythmias, and cinchonism (tinnitus, hearing impairment).

WHO guidelines mandate that all patients with severe malaria receive a minimum of 24 hours (at least 3 doses at 0, 12, and 24 hours) of IV or IM artesunate, followed by a full 3-day oral artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) once oral intake is tolerated.

page.mentor_intro: Differentiating Plasmodium species is critical for selecting therapy and eradicating dormant liver stages. Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) are the frontline standard for uncomplicated malaria, while primaquine or tafenoquine is essential for terminal radical cure in P. vivax and P. ovale.

teaching_points.claim: Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria should be treated with an oral artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) such as artemether-lumefantrine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for 3 days to ensure rapid parasite clearance and prevent resistance.

P. vivax and P. ovale form dormant hypnozoites in hepatocytes that cause late clinical relapses; radical cure requires 14 days of primaquine (or single-dose tafenoquine) following blood-stage antimalarial treatment.

Quantitative testing for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is mandatory prior to prescribing primaquine or tafenoquine to prevent life-threatening acute intravascular hemolytic anemia.
Severe malaria, regardless of the infecting Plasmodium species, mandates immediate treatment with intravenous artesunate (2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, and 24 hours) as established by the AQUAMAT trial.

page.mentor_intro: Male breast cancer is an uncommon malignancy accounting for approximately 1% of all breast cancers, characterized by high rates of hormone-receptor positivity and strong associations with inherited cancer syndromes. The ASCO clinical practice guideline establishes tamoxifen as the standard adjuvant endocrine therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The ASCO clinical practice guideline recommends tamoxifen for an initial duration of 5 years as the standard adjuvant endocrine therapy for men with hormone receptor-positive early-stage breast cancer.

Aromatase inhibitor monotherapy is not recommended in men with breast cancer because inhibiting peripheral aromatase without testicular suppression triggers a pituitary feedback loop that increases LH, FSH, and testicular androgen/estrogen production.

If an aromatase inhibitor is required due to contraindications or intolerance to tamoxifen, it must be co-administered with a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analog (e.g. leuprolide) to suppress testicular steroidogenesis.
Routine germline genetic counseling and testing for BRCA1 and especially BRCA2 mutations is recommended for all men diagnosed with breast cancer, regardless of age or family cancer history.

page.mentor_intro: Male hypogonadism results from testicular failure (primary) or hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction (secondary). Clinical practice guidelines from the Endocrine Society require confirmed morning hypogonadism on repeated testing, differentiation of primary from secondary etiologies, and structured hematocrit and prostate monitoring.

teaching_points.claim: Primary hypogonadism is characterized by low serum testosterone with elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) due to intrinsic testicular failure (e.g. Klinefelter syndrome 47,XXY, mumps orchitis, or bilateral testicular trauma).

Secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism features low testosterone with inappropriately low or normal LH and FSH, necessitating measurement of serum prolactin and iron studies (hemochromatosis), as well as pituitary MRI if prolactin is elevated or severe visual deficits exist.

The randomized TRAVERSE trial demonstrated that testosterone replacement therapy in hypogonadal men with pre-existing cardiovascular disease or high risk was noninferior to placebo for major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.96).
Baseline and surveillance monitoring during testosterone therapy requires serum hematocrit and PSA assessment at 3 to 6 months, with treatment held or dose reduced if hematocrit exceeds 54%.

page.mentor_intro: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) restores physiological androgen levels in men with pathological hypogonadism. Landmark evidence from the TRAVERSE trial has redefined clinical understanding of cardiovascular safety, while highlighting secondary risks including non-fatal arrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, and clinical fractures.

teaching_points.claim: The multicenter randomized TRAVERSE trial of 5,246 men established that testosterone replacement therapy does not increase the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke) over a median follow-up of 3.2 years.

The TRAVERSE fracture substudy revealed that testosterone therapy was unexpectedly associated with a higher incidence of all clinical fractures (HR 1.43) compared with placebo in middle-aged and older hypogonadal men.

Secondary safety analyses from the TRAVERSE trial demonstrated modest but statistically significant increases in the incidence of atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, and venous thromboembolic events in the testosterone group.

The Endocrine Society clinical guidelines advise against administering testosterone replacement therapy to men who have experienced an acute cardiovascular event (myocardial infarction or stroke) within the preceding 6 months.

page.mentor_intro: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a distressing complication of advanced intra-abdominal and pelvic malignancies, characterized by mechanical blockage, intestinal secretion, and visceral pain. Multinational guidelines prioritize medical palliation using somatostatin analogues (octreotide) and corticosteroids when surgical relief is not feasible.

teaching_points.claim: The MASCC clinical practice guidelines recommend the somatostatin analogue octreotide as the first-line antisecretory agent to reduce gastrointestinal secretions, nausea, vomiting, and colicky pain in inoperable malignant bowel obstruction.

A 3- to 5-day trial of parenteral corticosteroids (dexamethasone 6 to 16 mg daily) is recommended to reduce peritumoral inflammation and edema, facilitating spontaneous resolution or partial decompression in selected MBO cases.

Palliative surgical intervention (bypass, resection, or diverting stoma) or endoscopic self-expanding metal stenting (SEMS) is considered primarily for single-point localized obstructions in patients with good performance status and absence of carcinomatosis.

Prokinetic agents (such as metoclopramide) are strictly contraindicated in complete mechanical bowel obstruction due to the high risk of severe colic, bowel ischemia, and gastrointestinal perforation.

topic: Malignant hyperthermia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome: recognition and dantrolene

guidelinesKept: Consensus Guidelines on Malignant Hyperthermia and Dantrolene Availability from the European Malignant Hyperthermia Group

page.mentor_intro: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are life-threatening hypermetabolic emergencies characterized by severe hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability. The European Malignant Hyperthermia Group (EMHG) establishes protocols for rapid trigger removal and immediate intravenous dantrolene administration.

teaching_points.claim: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited pharmacogenetic myopathy triggered by volatile inhalational anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine due to mutations in the ryanodine receptor (RYR1) causing uncontrolled myoplasmic calcium release.

Immediate management of malignant hyperthermia requires discontinuing all triggering volatile agents, hyperventilating with 100% oxygen at high flows, and administering intravenous dantrolene at an initial dose of 2.0 to 2.5 mg/kg repeated as necessary.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is an idiosyncratic reaction triggered by central dopamine receptor antagonists (antipsychotics) characterized by 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, hyperthermia, autonomic instability, and marked creatine kinase elevation.

Management of NMS requires immediate cessation of the offending neuroleptic, supportive care, and consideration of adjunctive therapy with the dopamine agonist bromocriptine or dantrolene to reduce severe muscle hypermetabolism.
