topic: methotrexate early rheumatoid arthritis combination therapy TEAR

guidelinesKept: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2022 update

page.mentor_intro: Early aggressive treatment in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) prevents irreversible structural joint damage; comparative effectiveness trials show that conventional oral triple synthetic DMARD therapy achieves clinical disease control and radiographic non-inferiority comparable to biological anti-TNF combination regimens at substantially lower cost.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized double-blind TEAR trial, early aggressive combination therapy (oral triple therapy: methotrexate + sulfasalazine + hydroxychloroquine vs etanercept + methotrexate) produced immediate and equivalent disease activity score reductions (DAS28-ESR) and equivalent preservation of radiographic progression over 2 years.

The randomized Swefot trial confirmed that among early RA patients with inadequate response to methotrexate monotherapy at 3 months, addition of sulfasalazine and hydroxychloroquine (triple therapy) produced durable clinical responses comparable to biological anti-TNF addition through 24 months.

In the RACAT non-inferiority trial, oral triple therapy was clinically non-inferior to etanercept plus methotrexate in patients with active RA despite methotrexate monotherapy, with successful cross-over demonstrating that patients failing triple therapy responded effectively to anti-TNF rescue.

EULAR guidelines recommend starting conventional synthetic DMARD (csDMARD) monotherapy with methotrexate rapidly at RA diagnosis, with progression to csDMARD combination or biologic DMARD (bDMARD) therapy if treatment targets (remission or low disease activity) are not achieved by 3-6 months.

topic: Methotrexate in RA: dosing, folate supplementation, monitoring, toxicity

guidelinesKept: 2021 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis

page.mentor_intro: Methotrexate is the anchor synthetic DMARD for rheumatoid arthritis, requiring weekly oral or subcutaneous administration paired with mandatory folic acid supplementation, structured blood monitoring, and early recognition of hepatotoxic, hematologic, and pulmonary toxicities.

teaching_points.claim: ACR and EULAR guidelines recommend initiating oral methotrexate at 15 mg once weekly, escalating rapidly by 2.5-5 mg every 2-4 weeks to a target dose of 20-25 mg once weekly to establish disease control within the critical early therapeutic window.

A Cochrane systematic review confirmed that routine folic acid supplementation (5-10 mg weekly, taken 24-48 hours after MTX) reduces methotrexate-induced hepatic transaminitis by 73% (RR 0.27; 95% CI 0.17-0.44) and reduces gastrointestinal adverse events and trial discontinuation without impairing DMARD efficacy.

Switching from oral to subcutaneous methotrexate significantly improves bioavailability, bypasses gut saturable active transport mechanisms, and provides superior clinical efficacy with lower gastrointestinal toxicity in patients with inadequate response or intolerance to oral doses >=15 mg/week.

Safety monitoring requires baseline complete blood count, transaminases, and renal function, repeated every 2-4 weeks for the first 3 months, then every 8-12 weeks thereafter; transient transaminase elevations <3x upper limit of normal warrant dose reduction rather than permanent drug cessation.

guidelinesKept: American College of Rheumatology 2012 recommendations for the use of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs and biologic agents in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis

page.mentor_intro: Methotrexate toxicity spans idiosyncratic pulmonary hypersensitivity, cumulative hepatotoxicity, myelosuppression, and oncologic overdose nephrotoxicity, demanding structured surveillance protocols, urgent recognition of acute pneumonitis, and emergency rescue algorithms.

teaching_points.claim: In the large cardiovascular inflammation reduction trial (CIRT) evaluating 4,786 patients on low-dose methotrexate (15-20 mg/week), MTX caused modest elevations in liver enzymes, mild reductions in white blood cell counts, and an increased incidence of non-basal cell skin cancers without catastrophic liver failure or pulmonary fibrosis.

Acute methotrexate pneumonitis is an idiosyncratic, life-threatening hypersensitivity reaction presenting with subacute dry cough, dyspnea, fever, peripheral eosinophilia, and bilateral ground-glass opacities; it requires immediate and permanent discontinuation of methotrexate and high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

In high-dose oncology regimens (>=500 mg/m2), methotrexate precipitates in renal tubules causing acute kidney injury; prevention mandates vigorous intravenous hydration, urinary alkalinization to pH >=7.0, leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue, and emergent glucarpidase in refractory toxic accumulation.

Drug interactions with NSAIDs, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, penicillin, and proton pump inhibitors impair renal tubular secretion or displace methotrexate from albumin binding, precipitating severe myelosuppression.

page.mentor_intro: Vasoplegic shock following cardiopulmonary bypass is characterized by profound systemic hypotension refractory to high-dose catecholaminergic vasopressors; methylene blue restores systemic vascular resistance by selectively inhibiting inducible nitric oxide synthase and soluble guanylyl cyclase.

teaching_points.claim: In a randomized controlled trial by Levin and colleagues of patients developing vasoplegic syndrome after cardiac surgery, intravenous methylene blue (1.5 mg/kg infusion over 1 hour) produced rapid, sustained arterial blood pressure recovery and significantly reduced mortality (0% vs 21.4%; p=0.01) compared with placebo.

Methylene blue acts as an inhibitor of both inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), terminating excessive cyclic GMP generation and restoring vascular smooth muscle responsiveness to circulating catecholamines.

A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis by Lenglet and colleagues demonstrated that methylene blue administration in post-cardiac surgery vasoplegia was associated with a significant reduction in vasopressor requirements, shorter ICU stay, and decreased operative mortality.

Clinicians must recognize critical contraindications and toxicities: methylene blue is a potent monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) that can precipitate life-threatening serotonin syndrome when co-administered with serotonergic agents (SSRIs/SNRIs) and can trigger acute hemolysis in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.

topic: metoprolol succinate chronic heart failure mortality MERIT-HF

guidelinesKept: 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure

page.mentor_intro: Metoprolol succinate controlled-release/extended-release (CR/XL) is one of three guideline-directed beta-blockers proven to improve survival in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), reducing all-cause mortality, sudden cardiac death, and hospitalization.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark MERIT-HF randomized trial, metoprolol succinate CR/XL added to standard therapy in 3,991 patients with NYHA class II-IV heart failure and ejection fraction <=40% reduced all-cause mortality by 34% (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53-0.81; p=0.00009) and sudden death by 41%.

The COMET trial proved that the formulations are not interchangeable: carvedilol produced significantly superior survival compared to short-acting metoprolol tartrate, emphasizing that guideline-directed survival benefits are specific to metoprolol succinate CR/XL and cannot be extrapolated to metoprolol tartrate.

ESC and AHA/ACC guidelines mandate initiating metoprolol succinate at low doses (12.5-25 mg once daily) and titrating every 2 weeks toward the target dose of 200 mg once daily, as trial benefits were achieved at high target doses.

Cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic blockade reverses chronic sympathetic neurohormonal overdrive, suppresses ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and promotes reverse left ventricular remodeling with progressive recovery of ejection fraction.

page.mentor_intro: Methylene blue administration represents a targeted hemodynamic rescue therapy for refractory vasoplegic syndrome following cardiopulmonary bypass, arresting downstream cyclic GMP-mediated vasodilation through dual inhibition of nitric oxide synthase and soluble guanylyl cyclase.

teaching_points.claim: Randomized clinical trial evidence from Levin and colleagues established that early infusion of methylene blue (1.5 mg/kg over 1 hour) in patients with postcardiotomy vasoplegia resolved shock, shortened vasopressor duration from 71 to 17 hours, and eliminated vasoplegia-related mortality.

Vasoplegia in cardiac surgery involves pathological endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) upregulation, driving massive vascular smooth muscle cyclic GMP synthesis; methylene blue directly blocks sGC and scavenges nitric oxide.

Systematic reviews of rescue rescue therapy across refractory cardiac and septic shock indicate that methylene blue consistently elevates mean arterial pressure and systemic vascular resistance while reducing vasopressor dependency index.

Safety evaluation requires careful screening for concurrent serotonergic medications to prevent fatal serotonin syndrome, recognition of transient pulse oximeter interference, and avoidance in known G6PD deficiency due to Heinz body hemolytic anemia.

guidelinesKept: Guidelines on the diagnosis and management of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and other thrombotic microangiopathies

page.mentor_intro: Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (MAHA) is a clinicopathologic syndrome defined by red blood cell fragmentation (schistocytes on peripheral blood smear), severe thrombocytopenia, and microvascular thrombosis, requiring rapid diagnostic discrimination between thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized HERCULES trial, the anti-vWF nanobody caplacizumab added to plasma exchange and immunosuppression in immune TTP significantly reduced the time to platelet count response, reduced TTP-related deaths, recurrences, or thromboembolic events by 74% (12.7% vs 49.3%; p<0.001), and prevented refractoriness.

TTP is defined by severe deficiency of ADAMTS13 activity (<10%), while pre-test probability is rapidly quantified by the PLASMIC score; scores >=6 indicate high risk of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency and mandate immediate plasma exchange and corticosteroids without awaiting enzyme results.

Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is mediated by uncontrolled alternative complement pathway activation; early initiation of terminal complement C5 inhibitors (eculizumab or ravulizumab) halts complement-mediated endothelial injury, normalizes hematologic parameters, and recovers renal function.

Platelet transfusions are strictly contraindicated in suspected TTP unless life-threatening hemorrhage is present, because exogenous platelets fuel disseminated microvascular thrombosis and have precipitated acute myocardial infarction and stroke.

page.mentor_intro: Microscopic colitis, encompassing collagenous colitis and lymphocytic colitis, is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the large bowel characterized by chronic watery, non-bloody diarrhea and endoscopically normal colonic mucosa, definitively diagnosed by histopathological biopsy and treated primarily with oral budesonide.

teaching_points.claim: European Microscopic Colitis Group (EMCG) and AGA guidelines establish that colonoscopy with multiple mucosal biopsies (both right and left colon) is mandatory, as macroscopically the mucosal appearance is normal or near-normal despite extensive microscopic inflammation.

Histopathological hallmarks differentiate the two subtypes: collagenous colitis features a thickened subepithelial collagen band (>=10 micrometers), while lymphocytic colitis is defined by >=20 intraepithelial lymphocytes per 100 surface epithelial cells.

Cochrane systematic reviews demonstrate that oral budesonide (9 mg daily for 6-8 weeks) is the gold standard first-line treatment for induction of clinical remission (RR 7.35; 95% CI 2.43-22.2), significantly outperforming mesalazine or placebo.

Risk factors and triggers include female sex, age >60 years, concurrent autoimmune diseases (celiac disease, Hashimoto thyroiditis), and frequent culprit medications (NSAIDs, proton pump inhibitors, SSRIs, and statins) that should be discontinued upon diagnosis.

page.mentor_intro: Oral budesonide represents the evidence-based cornerstone for both induction and maintenance of clinical remission in microscopic colitis, providing localized colonic anti-inflammatory action with minimal systemic glucocorticoid adverse effects due to extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism.

teaching_points.claim: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Miehlke and colleagues, budesonide maintenance therapy (initially 6 mg daily, titrated to 3-4.5 mg daily) maintained clinical remission over 1 year in 61.4% of patients compared to 16.7% with placebo (HR 0.23; p=0.0002).

Bonderup and colleagues proved that 8 weeks of oral budesonide (9 mg/day) achieved significant histological remission, reduction of stool weight, and cessation of nocturnal diarrhea in collagenous colitis without adrenal suppression.

Following successful 8-week induction with budesonide 9 mg daily, approximately 60-80% of patients experience symptom recurrence upon cessation; EMCG guidelines recommend tapering to the lowest effective maintenance dose (3 mg daily or 3 mg on alternate days) for recurrent disease.

page.mentor_intro: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) is a systemic necrotizing pauci-immune small-vessel vasculitis strongly associated with myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA, characteristically manifesting as rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage, managed with remission-induction immunosuppression.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark RAVE trial, rituximab was non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for remission induction in severe ANCA-associated vasculitis (64% vs 53%) and was significantly superior to cyclophosphamide for induction in patients presenting with relapsing disease (67% vs 42%; p=0.01).

The randomized PEXIVAS trial demonstrated that plasma exchange did not reduce the incidence of end-stage kidney disease or death (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.65-1.13) in patients with severe ANCA-associated vasculitis with renal impairment or pulmonary hemorrhage, while a reduced-dose glucocorticoid regimen was non-inferior to standard-dose glucocorticoids with fewer serious infections.

In the ADVOCATE trial, the oral complement C5a receptor antagonist avacopan proved superior to a standard prednisone taper in achieving sustained remission at 52 weeks (65.7% vs 54.9%; p=0.007) while significantly enhancing eGFR recovery and reducing glucocorticoid toxicity.

Unlike granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), MPA typically lacks granulomatous upper respiratory tract inflammation and pulmonary cavitary nodules, and is predominantly characterized by perinuclear (p-ANCA) staining targeting myeloperoxidase (MPO).

page.mentor_intro: Migraine is a prevalent neurovascular brain disorder characterized by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe throbbing headache associated with photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, and in one-third of individuals, transient focal neurological aura, managed by acute stratified analgesia and proactive preventive therapies.

teaching_points.claim: According to ICHD-3 criteria, migraine without aura requires at least 5 attacks lasting 4-72 hours, with >=2 pain characteristics (unilateral, pulsating, moderate/severe, aggravated by routine physical activity) and >=1 associated symptom (nausea/vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia).

In systematic reviews and meta-analyses by Ferrari and colleagues, oral 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists (triptans: rizatriptan, eletriptan, sumatriptan) demonstrated robust 2-hour headache relief (59-67%) and pain-free response, outperforming ergotamines and analgesics when administered early in the headache phase.

American Headache Society guidelines recommend initiating preventive pharmacotherapy when patients experience >=4 headache days per month, debilitating attacks despite acute therapy, or are at risk of medication-overuse headache from taking acute analgesics >=10-15 days per month.

First-line conventional preventive options with established Level A evidence include beta-blockers without intrinsic sympathomimetic activity (propranolol, metoprolol), topiramate, and amitriptyline, while gepants (rimegepant, atogepant) and anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies offer targeted non-vasoconstrictive alternatives.

page.mentor_intro: Monoclonal antibodies targeting calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) or its canonical receptor (erenumab, galcanezumab, fremanezumab, eptinezumab) represent targeted, disease-specific preventive therapies for episodic and chronic migraine, demonstrating rapid onset of efficacy, sustained reduction in migraine days, and favorable adverse effect profiles.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 STRIVE trial, monthly subcutaneous erenumab (targeting the canonical CGRP receptor complex) significantly reduced monthly migraine days by 3.7 days (70 mg) and 4.0 days (140 mg) compared with 1.8 days for placebo, with >=50% reduction achieved by 50% of patients.

The phase 3 EVOLVE-1 and EVOLVE-2 randomized trials demonstrated that galcanezumab (targeting the CGRP ligand) produced statistically significant, clinically meaningful reductions in monthly migraine headache days and acute medication use days across 6 months in episodic migraine.

In chronic migraine (>=15 headache days/month), the PROMISE-2 trial demonstrated that quarterly intravenous eptinezumab produced significant migraine day reductions starting from day 1 post-infusion through week 24, with favorable tolerability and high patient compliance.

Because CGRP inhibitors do not cause vascular smooth muscle constriction, they do not carry the vasoconstrictive ischemic contraindications of triptans or ergot alkaloids, though post-marketing surveillance identifies severe constipation and worsening hypertension as potential risks with erenumab.

topic: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI): amnestic vs non-amnestic progression tracking

guidelinesKept: Practice guideline update summary: Mild cognitive impairment

page.mentor_intro: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents an intermediate cognitive state between normal cognitive aging and dementia, characterized by objective cognitive decline on formal testing without substantial impairment in independence of daily living, progressing to Alzheimer's disease dementia at 10-15% per year.

teaching_points.claim: According to the American Academy of Neurology (AAN) practice guideline update, clinicians should assess patients with suspected cognitive decline using validated brief cognitive assessment tools (e.g., MoCA) and avoid prescribing acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, which have no proven efficacy in delaying dementia conversion in MCI.

MCI is clinically stratified into amnestic MCI (prominent episodic memory impairment, most commonly progressing to Alzheimer's dementia) and non-amnestic MCI (impairments in executive function, language, or visuospatial domains, which more frequently convert to dementia with Lewy bodies, frontotemporal lobar degeneration, or vascular dementia).

The NIA-AA ATN biomarker research framework incorporates cerebrospinal fluid or PET imaging biomarkers of amyloid-beta deposition (A), hyperphosphorylated tau (T), and neurodegeneration (N) to establish the biological etiology and risk of rapid progression in individuals with amnestic MCI.

Non-pharmacological management with structured physical aerobic exercise (twice weekly for 6 months) demonstrates modest cognitive benefits, and AAN guidelines recommend discussing exercise, cognitive stimulation, and cardiovascular risk factor optimization.

topic: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in heart failure

page.mentor_intro: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are foundational neurohormonal inhibitors in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), blocking aldosterone-mediated myocardial fibrosis and electrical instability to produce substantial reductions in sudden cardiac death and all-cause mortality.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark RALES trial, the addition of spironolactone (mean dose 26 mg daily) to standard therapy in patients with severe HFrEF (NYHA class III-IV, LVEF <=35%) reduced all-cause mortality by 30% (RR 0.70; 95% CI 0.60-0.82; p<0.001) and cardiac hospitalization by 35%.

The EMPHASIS-HF trial demonstrated that the selective MRA eplerenone (up to 50 mg daily) in patients with mild systolic heart failure (NYHA class II, LVEF <=35%) reduced cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by 37% (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.54-0.74; p<0.001).

In post-myocardial infarction LV systolic dysfunction (LVEF <=40% and clinical HF or diabetes), the EPHESUS trial showed that eplerenone significantly reduced all-cause mortality by 15% (RR 0.85; p=0.008) and sudden cardiac death by 21%.

In heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), the TOPCAT trial showed that spironolactone did not significantly reduce the overall primary composite cardiovascular endpoint, although prespecified regional analysis in the Americas demonstrated a significant 18% reduction.

topic: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists: spironolactone, eplerenone, finerenone

page.mentor_intro: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists encompass steroidal agents (spironolactone, eplerenone) with established HFrEF mortality benefits, and next-generation selective nonsteroidal agents (finerenone) that selectively suppress cardiorenal inflammation and fibrosis in diabetic kidney disease with lower hyperkalemia risk.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 FIDELIO-DKD trial, finerenone significantly reduced the primary composite kidney outcome (kidney failure, sustained >=40% eGFR decline, or renal death) by 18% (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.73-0.93; p=0.001) in patients with CKD and type 2 diabetes.

The FIGARO-DKD trial demonstrated that finerenone significantly reduced the composite cardiovascular outcome (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or heart failure hospitalization) by 13% (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.76-0.98; p=0.03) in patients with type 2 diabetes across less advanced CKD stages (stages 2-4 with albuminuria).

Nonsteroidal MRAs like finerenone have a balanced renal-cardiac distribution, higher mineralocorticoid receptor binding affinity than spironolactone or eplerenone, lack affinity for androgen and progesterone receptors (eliminating gynecomastia), and carry a lower risk of severe hyperkalemia.

A landmark population-based study by Juurlink and colleagues revealed that widespread adoption of spironolactone following RALES was accompanied by a dramatic surge in hospitalizations and deaths from hyperkalemia, underscoring the mandatory requirement for structured biochemical monitoring within 1-2 weeks of initiation.

page.mentor_intro: Minimal change disease (MCD) is the predominant cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and accounts for 10-15% of adult nephrotic syndrome, defined by normal light microscopy, absent immune complexes on immunofluorescence, and diffuse podocyte foot process effacement on electron microscopy, responding dramatically to high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

teaching_points.claim: KDIGO 2024 glomerular disease guidelines recommend high-dose oral corticosteroids (prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, maximum 80 mg/day, or alternate-day 2 mg/kg, maximum 120 mg) as initial therapy, continued until complete remission is achieved or for up to 16 weeks in adults.

Adults with MCD exhibit slower response kinetics than children: while over 80% achieve complete remission, median time to remission is 7 to 9 weeks, and frequent relapses or steroid dependence occur in over 50-70% of adult patients.

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Iijima and colleagues, rituximab significantly extended time to relapse and reduced steroid exposure in complicated, frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome.

For steroid-dependent or frequently relapsing disease, second-line immunosuppressive agents with proven steroid-sparing efficacy include cyclophosphamide, calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine), mycophenolate mofetil, and anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies (rituximab).

page.mentor_intro: Measurable/minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring quantifies persistent submicroscopic malignant clones using high-sensitivity multiparameter flow cytometry or next-generation sequencing, serving as the strongest surrogate biomarker for progression-free and overall survival in hematologic malignancies.

teaching_points.claim: In the prospective MASTER trial, daratumumab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (Dara-KRD) paired with autologous transplant and MRD-response-adapted therapy demonstrated that achieving confirmed MRD negativity (<10^-5 by NGS) allowed safe treatment cessation without early disease progression.

A comprehensive meta-analysis of over 8,000 multiple myeloma patients by Munshi and colleagues confirmed that achieving MRD negativity was associated with a 59% reduction in the risk of disease progression (HR 0.41; p<0.001) and a 43% reduction in death (HR 0.57; p<0.001), regardless of baseline cytogenetic risk.

In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), European LeukemiaNet (ELN) consensus guidelines establish that post-induction MRD assessment (by multiparameter flow cytometry or qPCR for NPM1/CBF fusions) provides superior prognostic discrimination compared to conventional morphological remission, guiding the decision for allogeneic stem cell transplantation in CR1.

In acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), meta-analyses by Berry and colleagues proved that post-induction MRD negativity (<10^-4) is the single most powerful prognostic factor for event-free survival in both pediatric (HR 0.23) and adult (HR 0.28) populations.

topic: MINOCA: ischaemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries workup and management

guidelinesKept: ESC working group position paper on myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)

page.mentor_intro: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome diagnosed in 6-10% of acute myocardial infarctions, characterized by evidence of acute myocardial necrosis and coronary angiography showing <50% stenosis, necessitating multimodality imaging and tailored secondary prevention.

teaching_points.claim: ESC and AHA guidelines define MINOCA by 3 mandatory criteria: acute myocardial infarction criteria (positive cardiac biomarkers with ischemic symptoms/ECG changes), non-obstructive coronary arteries on angiography (no epicardial stenosis >=50%), and no clinically overt alternative non-ischemic cause (e.g., severe sepsis, acute pulmonary embolism).

In the landmark HARP study by Reynolds and colleagues utilizing coronary optical coherence tomography (OCT) and cardiac MRI, an underlying etiology was definitively identified in 84.5% of women with MINOCA, with ischemic mechanisms (plaque rupture, plaque erosion, spasm) found in 64% and non-ischemic causes (myocarditis, Takotsubo) in 20.5%.

Early cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging (optimally performed within 1-2 weeks of presentation) is the cornerstone diagnostic investigation, distinguishing subendocardial ischemic necrosis from mid-wall/subepicardial myocarditis and non-ischemic Takotsubo syndrome.

In the nationwide SWEDEHEART registry of over 9,000 MINOCA patients, long-term secondary prevention with statins (HR 0.77; p<0.001) and ACE inhibitors / ARBs (HR 0.82; p<0.001) significantly reduced major adverse cardiac events, whereas dual antiplatelet therapy showed neutral benefit in unselected cohorts.

guidelinesKept: NICE NG126: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management

page.mentor_intro: Early pregnancy loss affects 15-20% of recognized pregnancies; accurate ultrasound confirmation based on strict quantitative dimensional criteria avoids premature intervention in viable intrauterine pregnancies, while contemporary management encompasses expectant, medical (mifepristone plus misoprostol), or surgical pathways.

teaching_points.claim: In the multicenter MifeMiso trial, pre-treatment with oral mifepristone (200 mg) followed 48 hours later by misoprostol (800 mcg) in women with missed miscarriage significantly increased the rate of complete miscarriage without surgery (83% vs 76%; RR 1.48; 95% CI 1.05-2.09) compared with misoprostol alone.

NICE NG126 guidelines mandate strict transvaginal ultrasound diagnostic thresholds to confirm non-viability: crown-rump length (CRL) >=7 mm with absent fetal heartbeat, or mean sac diameter (MSD) >=25 mm with absent embryo; if measurements are below these thresholds, a repeat scan in 7-14 days is mandatory.

In the PRISM randomized trial, vaginal micronized progesterone (400 mg twice daily) did not significantly increase live births in unselected women with early pregnancy bleeding, but produced a significant benefit in the prespecified subgroup of women with bleeding and >=1 prior miscarriages (75% vs 70% live birth rate; p=0.003 for >=3 prior miscarriages).

Anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis is recommended by NICE for all non-sensitized RhD-negative women undergoing surgical evacuation of pregnancy or medical management of miscarriage after 10 weeks gestation.

page.mentor_intro: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) using the MitraClip device improves survival and quality of life in secondary (functional) mitral regurgitation when mitral insufficiency is disproportionate to left ventricular dilatation and patients remain symptomatic despite maximal guideline-directed medical therapy.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark COAPT trial, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair added to maximal guideline-directed medical therapy in heart failure patients with moderate-to-severe or severe secondary mitral regurgitation significantly reduced 2-year heart failure hospitalizations (35.8% vs 67.9%; HR 0.53; p<0.001) and reduced 2-year all-cause mortality (29.1% vs 46.1%; HR 0.62; p<0.001).

Conversely, the MITRA-FR trial showed no significant benefit of TEER on 12-month mortality or heart failure hospitalization, highlighting critical patient selection differences reconciled by Grayburn's 'disproportionate MR' framework (COAPT: effective regurgitant orifice area EROA ~40 mm2 with LV end-diastolic volume index <100 mL/m2 vs MITRA-FR: EROA ~30 mm2 with severe LV dilatation >135 mL/m2).

ESC and ACC/AHA guidelines restrict TEER recommendation (Class I/IIa) in secondary MR strictly to patients who fulfill COAPT inclusion criteria: symptomatic NYHA II-IV despite optimized GDMT (including CRT if indicated), LVEF 20-50%, LV end-systolic dimension <=70 mm, and suitable mitral anatomy confirmed by Heart Team evaluation.

In primary (degenerative) mitral regurgitation, surgical mitral valve repair remains the standard Class I indication; TEER is reserved for symptomatic patients with severe primary MR deemed inoperable or at high surgical risk by a multidisciplinary Heart Team.

topic: Mitral stenosis: commissurotomy vs valve replacement, rheumatic disease

guidelinesKept: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease

page.mentor_intro: Rheumatic mitral stenosis causes progressive mechanical obstruction of left ventricular inflow; intervention is indicated for severe symptomatic stenosis (mitral valve area <=1.5 cm2) or pulmonary hypertension, with percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (PMBC) serving as first-line therapy when the Wilkins echocardiographic score is favorable.

teaching_points.claim: The Wilkins echocardiographic score grades mitral valve leaflet mobility, leaflet thickening, subvalvular thickening, and calcification from 1 to 4 (total 4 to 16); scores <=8 predict high procedural success and low restenosis rates following percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (PMBC).

In a landmark 20-year follow-up of 1,024 patients by Bouleti and colleagues, PMBC achieved immediate procedural success in 89% of patients, conferring durable long-term functional survival with freedom from reintervention in 56% at 10 years and 30% at 20 years in anatomically suitable candidates.

ACC/AHA and ESC guidelines recommend PMBC as Class I first-line treatment for symptomatic severe rheumatic mitral stenosis (mitral valve area MVA <=1.5 cm2) in the absence of left atrial thrombus or moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation.

Surgical mitral valve replacement is mandated when Wilkins score is >8-10, bicommissural calcification is present, severe mitral regurgitation coexists, or a persistent left atrial appendage thrombus is detected on transesophageal echocardiography despite therapeutic anticoagulation.

guidelinesKept: Classification and diagnostic criteria for mixed connective tissue disease

page.mentor_intro: Mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) is an autoimmune overlap syndrome characterized by high titers of circulating antibodies to U1-small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (anti-U1-RNP) alongside overlapping clinical features of systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis.

teaching_points.claim: According to the Alarcón-Segovia and Kasukawa diagnostic criteria, definitive diagnosis of MCTD requires high-titer anti-U1-RNP antibodies in the absence of anti-Sm or anti-dsDNA antibodies, accompanied by clinical features spanning Raynaud's phenomenon, swollen hands/puffy fingers, synovitis, myositis, or esophageal dysmotility.

In nationwide prospective registry studies by Gunnarsson and colleagues, Raynaud's phenomenon was present in >95% and swollen 'puffy' fingers in >80% of patients, representing the classic early clinical presentation.

Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is the leading cause of disease-related mortality in MCTD (accounting for >40% of deaths), developing insidiously and often independently of active systemic inflammatory features.

Immunosuppressive treatment is tailored to organ manifestations: low-dose corticosteroids and hydroxychloroquine manage mild articular and mucocutaneous symptoms, whereas severe inflammatory myositis, interstitial lung disease, or glomerulonephritis require high-dose corticosteroids combined with cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, or azathioprine.

guidelinesKept: 2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension

page.mentor_intro: Pulmonary involvement in mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) is the primary determinant of long-term survival, encompassing pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and interstitial lung disease (ILD), necessitating proactive annual screening with transthoracic echocardiography and pulmonary function testing.

teaching_points.claim: In a nationwide prospective cohort study by Gunnarsson and colleagues, pulmonary arterial hypertension occurred in 3.4% of MCTD patients and accounted for the majority of disease-related deaths, carrying a 3-year survival rate under 65% in the pre-modern therapy era.

ESC/ERS guidelines recommend annual screening for pulmonary hypertension in patients with MCTD using transthoracic echocardiography and measurement of diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO).

A disproportionate reduction in DLCO (<70% predicted) with preserved forced vital capacity (FVC) or an elevated FVC/DLCO ratio >1.6 strongly signals underlying pulmonary vascular disease (PAH) rather than isolated parenchymal interstitial lung disease.

Contemporary management of MCTD-associated PAH combines immunosuppressive therapy (cyclophosphamide or mycophenolate mofetil with glucocorticoids) with upfront combination pulmonary vasodilators (endothelin receptor antagonists and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors).

topic: MODY: HNF1A GCK HNF4A subtypes - genetic testing and treatment implications

page.mentor_intro: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) is an autosomal dominant monogenic form of non-ketotic beta-cell dysfunction; genetic identification of specific mutations (GCK, HNF1A, HNF4A) directly transforms clinical care, allowing safe cessation of insulin or low-dose sulfonylurea monotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: In patients with HNF1A-MODY (MODY3), a randomized crossover trial by Pearson and colleagues proved that patients exhibit exquisite sensitivity to low-dose oral sulfonylureas, achieving 4-fold greater glycemic response than patients with type 2 diabetes and allowing successful discontinuation of insulin.

Steele and colleagues demonstrated that patients with GCK-MODY (MODY2) have a regulated resetting of the glucose sensor producing lifelong mild stable fasting hyperglycemia (5.5-8.0 mmol/L, HbA1c 5.6-7.3%) that does not cause microvascular complications and requires no pharmacological therapy.

The Exeter MODY probability calculator incorporates age of onset <35 years, positive family history, absence of ketoacidosis, absence of obesity/metabolic syndrome, and persistent detectable C-peptide to identify individuals who warrant targeted next-generation sequencing.
HNF4A-MODY (MODY1) causes macrosomia and transient hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia in neonates followed by progressive adolescent/adult-onset diabetes that responds favorably to sulfonylureas.

topic: mog antibody associated disease diagnosis and relapse prevention

guidelinesKept: Diagnosis of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease: International MOGAD Consortium proposed criteria

page.mentor_intro: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a distinct autoimmune demyelinating central nervous system disorder characterized by antibodies against conformational MOG, manifesting as optic neuritis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), or transverse myelitis, diagnosed by live cell-based assays and managed with acute immunotherapy and prolonged steroid tapers.

teaching_points.claim: According to the 2023 International MOGAD Consortium diagnostic criteria, diagnosis requires a core clinical demyelinating syndrome (optic neuritis, ADEM, myelitis, brainstem encephalitis, cerebral cortical encephalitis), exclusion of alternative diagnoses, and clear positive MOG-IgG tested by cell-based assay.
Cell-based assays (CBA) expressing full-length human MOG are mandatory; ELISA and Western blot assays produce unacceptably high false-positive rates and must not be used for clinical decision-making.

In a multicenter study by Chen and colleagues, oral corticosteroid tapers lasting >=3 months following acute demyelination significantly reduced the hazard of relapse compared to shorter tapers (<1 month), establishing the necessity of prolonged tapering.

Relapse prevention in patients with recurrent relapsing MOGAD involves steroid-sparing maintenance immunosuppression: regular intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) infusions, rituximab, or azathioprine significantly reduce annualized relapse rates.

topic: MOG antibody-associated disease diagnosis and relapse prevention

guidelinesKept: Diagnosis of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease: International MOGAD Consortium proposed criteria

page.mentor_intro: MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) exhibits distinct immunopathological features that differentiate it from aquaporin-4-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) and multiple sclerosis, demanding cell-based antibody confirmation, prompt high-dose corticosteroid rescue, and maintenance immunotherapy for relapsing disease.

teaching_points.claim: The International MOGAD Consortium 2023 criteria differentiate MOGAD from AQP4-positive NMOSD and MS, establishing that spinal cord involvement characteristically manifests as longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) involving the central cord and conus medullaris.

Cell-based assay (CBA) serology with high-titer MOG-IgG (>=1:100) or low-titer positivity paired with supporting clinical and MRI features (e.g., optic perineuritis, bilateral optic nerve lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis) confirms diagnosis.

Observational cohort studies by Hacohen and colleagues demonstrated that regular monthly intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) significantly reduced relapse rates in relapsing pediatric and adult MOGAD, demonstrating superior efficacy compared with conventional MS disease-modifying drugs.

Traditional multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapies (interferon-beta, glatiramer acetate, natalizumab, fingolimod) are ineffective and can paradoxically exacerbate disease activity in patients with MOGAD.

page.mentor_intro: Comprehensive biomarker testing in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) adenocarcinoma is an essential standard of care; broad-panel next-generation sequencing (NGS) and reflex PD-L1 immunohistochemistry identify actionable oncogenic drivers to guide first-line precision targeted therapy.

teaching_points.claim: CAP/IASLC/AMP and ESMO clinical guidelines mandate testing for all guideline-recommended oncogenic drivers in advanced pulmonary adenocarcinoma before initiating first-line systemic therapy: EGFR mutations, ALK fusions, ROS1 fusions, BRAF V600E, RET rearrangements, MET exon 14 skipping, KRAS G12C, NTRK1-3 fusions, and HER2 insertions.

Multiplex next-generation sequencing (NGS) utilizing DNA and RNA hybrid capture is the preferred diagnostic modality over sequential single-gene testing, as NGS maximizes tissue preservation, prevents tissue exhaustion, and optimizes detection of complex structural RNA fusions (ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK).

In the landmark KEYNOTE-024 trial, first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy in advanced NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations and with PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) >=50% significantly prolonged progression-free and overall survival compared to platinum-doublet chemotherapy (HR 0.60; p=0.005).

ESMO guidelines emphasize that when an actionable oncogenic driver (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, RET) is identified, targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors take precedence as first-line therapy regardless of high PD-L1 expression, as immune checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy yields negligible response rates and increases toxicity in oncogene-addicted tumors.

page.mentor_intro: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is a premalignant clonal plasma cell or lymphoplasmacytic proliferative disorder present in >3% of individuals over 50 years, progressing to multiple myeloma or related lymphoproliferative malignancies at a constant rate of 1% per year.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark 50-year Olmsted County follow-up study of 1,384 MGUS patients by Kyle and colleagues, the overall risk of progression to multiple myeloma or related plasma-cell disorders was 1% per year, and this risk persisted indefinitely without plateauing even after 35 years of observation.

The Mayo Clinic risk-stratification model identifies three independent progression predictors: serum M-protein concentration >=15 g/L, non-IgG isotype (IgA or IgM), and an abnormal serum free light chain (FLC) kappa/lambda ratio (<0.26 or >1.65); patients with all 3 risk factors have a 20-year progression risk of 58% vs 5% for zero risk factors.

Diagnostic criteria require serum monoclonal protein <30 g/L, bone marrow clonal plasma cells <10%, and the absolute absence of CRAB end-organ damage (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, or lytic bone lesions attributable to plasma cell proliferative disorder).

Prospective cohort studies from the PLCO screening trial demonstrated that an asymptomatic MGUS phase virtually always precedes the development of clinical multiple myeloma, confirming MGUS as an obligatory precursor stage.

page.mentor_intro: Monocytosis and lymphocytosis demand structured diagnostic algorithms distinguishing reactive polyclonal responses from clonal hematologic malignancies, utilizing peripheral blood smear review, multiparameter flow cytometry, and targeted next-generation sequencing.

teaching_points.claim: According to the 2022 International Consensus Classification (ICC) and WHO guidelines, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) requires persistent peripheral blood monocytosis (>=0.5 x 10^9/L and monocytes constituting >=10% of total white blood cell count), along with bone marrow dysplasia or characteristic clonal cytogenetic/molecular mutations.

Diagnostic evaluation of persistent monocytosis (>3 months) requires flow cytometric quantification of classical monocyte subsets (CD14++CD16-), where a classical monocyte proportion >=94% demonstrates high diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for CMML.

In adults presenting with absolute lymphocytosis (>5.0 x 10^9/L), peripheral blood multiparameter flow cytometry is the essential first-line test, identifying clonal B-cell populations expressing CD5, CD19, CD20 (dim), CD23, and light chain restriction to confirm chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL).

Monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL) is distinguished from CLL by an absolute circulating clonal B-cell count <5.0 x 10^9/L in the absence of lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, cytopenias, or disease-related constitutional symptoms.

topic: Mononeuritis multiplex: vasculitic causes, nerve biopsy indications

page.mentor_intro: Mononeuritis multiplex is an asymmetric, asynchronous painful sensorimotor polyneuropathy involving multiple non-contiguous individual peripheral nerves, most frequently caused by systemic necrotizing vasculitis, requiring urgent electrodiagnostic confirmation, targeted nerve biopsy, and prompt immunosuppression.

teaching_points.claim: Peripheral Nerve Society consensus guidelines state that mononeuritis multiplex presenting with rapid, painful stepwise nerve deficits represents a medical emergency caused by ischemic infarction of the vasa nervorum from systemic necrotizing vasculitis (e.g., GPA, MPA, EGPA, PAN, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis).

Combined superficial peroneal nerve and peroneus brevis muscle biopsy significantly increases diagnostic sensitivity for systemic and non-systemic vasculitic neuropathy to over 80% compared with isolated sensory nerve biopsy, while minimizing motor deficit.

Cochrane systematic review evidence demonstrates that aggressive first-line immunosuppression with high-dose corticosteroids (intravenous pulse methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone) combined with cyclophosphamide or rituximab arrests axonal infarction and prevents permanent motor disability.

Nerve conduction studies demonstrate asymmetric, non-uniform axonal sensory-motor neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potential (CMAP) and sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitudes, distinguishing vasculitic neuropathy from demyelinating polyneuropathies like CIDP or MMN.

page.mentor_intro: Morbilliform (maculopapular) exanthem is the most common cutaneous drug reaction, characterized by symmetric erythematous macules and papules developing 7 to 14 days after drug exposure, requiring rapid differentiation from life-threatening severe cutaneous adverse reactions such as DRESS, SJS/TEN, and AGEP.

teaching_points.claim: Exanthematous drug eruptions typically appear 7 to 14 days after starting a new medication (or within 1-2 days upon rechallenge), characteristically originating on the trunk and proximal extremities before spreading symmetrically and centrifugally with pruritus and low-grade or absent fever.

The RegiSCAR validation scoring system differentiates uncomplicated morbilliform drug rashes from Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) based on fever >=38.5 C, enlarged lymph nodes (>=2 sites), atypical lymphocytes, eosinophilia, and internal organ involvement (hepatic, renal, pulmonary, or cardiac).

Critical clinical red flags signaling a life-threatening severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR) include mucosal involvement (erosions of oral, ocular, or genital mucosa), cutaneous pain or tenderness, epidermal detachment/blistering (positive Nikolsky sign), facial edema, and palpable purpura.

DRESS syndrome frequently involves late reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHV-6, HHV-7, EBV, CMV) and demonstrates prolonged, relapsing systemic inflammation that persists for weeks to months despite discontinuation of the culprit drug, requiring prolonged oral corticosteroid tapers.

topic: Moyamoya disease: clinical presentations, surgical revascularisation indications

page.mentor_intro: Moyamoya disease is a progressive, occlusive cerebrovascular arteriopathy of the terminal internal carotid arteries and circle of Willis accompanied by compensatory fragile basal collateral vessels ('puffs of smoke'), causing recurrent ischemic stroke in children and intracranial hemorrhage in adults.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized multicenter JAM trial by Miyamoto and colleagues, extracranial-intracranial (EC-IC) direct arterial bypass surgery (superficial temporal artery to middle cerebral artery, STA-MCA) significantly reduced the incidence of recurrent hemorrhagic stroke from 31.6% in the non-surgical arm down to 11.9% (HR 0.35; p=0.042) in adult moyamoya disease.

Angiographic evaluation adheres to the 6 Suzuki stages, progressing from initial carotid fork stenosis (Stage 1), expansion of basal moyamoya collateral vessels (Stages 2-3), to progressive collateral regression and reliance on transdural external carotid collaterals (Stages 5-6).

Bimodal age distribution dictates distinct clinical presentations: pediatric patients (peak age ~5-10 years) present predominantly with ischemic transient ischemic attacks or infarctions triggered by hyperventilation (crying, blowing on hot food), whereas adults (peak age ~40-45 years) present with ischemic stroke or intraventricular/subarachnoid hemorrhage from rupture of fragile collateral microaneurysms.

Surgical revascularization strategies combine direct bypass (STA-MCA anastomosis, providing immediate augmentation of cerebral blood flow) and indirect bypass (encephalo-duro-arterio-synangiosis [EDAS] or pial synangiosis, which promotes neoangiogenesis over months, especially effective in pediatric populations).

guidelinesKept: Management of myeloproliferative neoplasm in blast phase: a consensus report from the MPN Research Consortium

page.mentor_intro: Progression of myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, myelofibrosis) to the blast phase (MPN-BP) is defined by >=20% blasts in peripheral blood or bone marrow; it represents a biologically aggressive acute myeloid leukemia with dismal prognosis, managed by hypomethylating agent combinations as a bridge to allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.

teaching_points.claim: According to the MPN Research Consortium consensus statement, MPN blast phase (MPN-BP) is defined by >=20% blasts in bone marrow or blood and carries a median overall survival under 6 months with standard supportive care or conventional induction chemotherapy.

In multi-institutional cohort studies by Badar and colleagues, hypomethylating agents (azacitidine or decitabine) combined with the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax achieved superior overall response rates (40-50%) and improved median survival compared with intensive 7+3 anthracycline-cytarabine chemotherapy (which carries excessive induction mortality >20-30%).

Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) remains the only curative therapy; patients who achieve an objective morphological blast clearance (<5% blasts) prior to transplant achieve durable 3-year post-transplant survival of 30-40%.

Passamonti and colleagues identified independent risk factors for leukemic transformation in primary myelofibrosis, including circulating blast count >=3%, platelet count <100 x 10^9/L, and high molecular risk (HMR) mutations (ASXL1, SRSF2, IDH1/2, EZH2).

topic: Mpox (monkeypox): transmission, clinical features, tecovirimat, vaccination, public health response

guidelinesKept: Tecovirimat (TPOXX) expanded access protocol and safety for mpox treatment

page.mentor_intro: Mpox (formerly monkeypox) is an orthopoxvirus zoonosis that caused a declared Public Health Emergency of International Concern in 2022-2023, transmitted predominantly through close physical and sexual contact, presenting with painful mucosal and cutaneous lesions, managed with supportive care, targeted tecovirimat, and MVA-BN vaccination.

teaching_points.claim: In an international collaborative study across 16 countries by Thornhill and colleagues, 98% of persons with mpox infection during the 2022-2023 outbreak were gay or bisexual men, with transmission occurring via close physical and sexual contact in 95%, presenting with anogenital mucosal lesions (73%), proctitis, and painful pharyngitis.

Diagnostic confirmation requires polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of swab specimens obtained directly from the base or exudate of cutaneous or mucosal lesions; serological testing lacks specificity due to orthopoxvirus cross-reactivity.

Tecovirimat (TPOXX), which inhibits the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope wrapping protein, is indicated under expanded access protocols for severe disease (extensive mucosal involvement, severe proctitis, ocular disease, or immunosuppression, particularly advanced HIV with CD4 <200 cells/mm3).

The modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN / JYNNEOS) replication-deficient vaccine demonstrated high real-world vaccine effectiveness, with CDC data showing a 14-fold higher incidence of infection in unvaccinated persons compared to those receiving the 2-dose subcutaneous series.

topic: MRI in inflammatory arthritis: bone marrow oedema, erosions, tenosynovitis scoring

page.mentor_intro: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a sensitive imaging modality in inflammatory arthritis, detecting subclinical synovitis, tenosynovitis, and bone marrow edema (osteitis) months before structural erosions appear on conventional plain radiography.

teaching_points.claim: The Rheumatoid Arthritis MRI Score (RAMRIS) system validated by OMERACT standardizes evaluation of the wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints, semi-quantitatively grading bone marrow edema (osteitis), synovitis, and bone erosion.

Bone marrow edema (osteitis) on fat-suppressed T2-weighted or short tau inversion recovery (STIR) sequences represents true histological intra-osseous inflammatory cellular infiltration and is the single strongest imaging predictor of subsequent bone erosion at that exact anatomical site.

In rheumatoid arthritis patients in clinical remission according to conventional disease activity scores (DAS28), high-resolution MRI reveals persistent subclinical synovitis and tenosynovitis in over 70% of patients, predicting disease flare and progressive structural damage.

In axial spondyloarthritis, the SPARCC scoring system quantifies bone marrow edema reflecting acute sacroiliitis, where active subchondral inflammation is required to meet ASAS criteria for non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA).

page.mentor_intro: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia carries high 30-day mortality (>20%) and metastatic seeding risk; management requires prompt focus control, echocardiographic screening, and targeted bactericidal antimicrobial therapy with vancomycin (monitored by AUC/MIC) or daptomycin.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized CAMERA2 trial, adding an antistaphylococcal beta-lactam (flucloxacillin or cefazolin) to standard therapy with vancomycin or daptomycin in MRSA bacteremia did not improve 90-day mortality (35% vs 32%; p=0.42) and was terminated early due to a significant excess in acute kidney injury (23% vs 6%; p<0.001).

IDSA and consensus guidelines recommend target vancomycin 24-hour area under the curve to minimum inhibitory concentration (AUC24/MIC) ratios of 400 to 600 mg*h/L using Bayesian dosing software, replacing traditional trough-only monitoring (15-20 mcg/mL) to reduce nephrotoxicity while preserving bactericidal efficacy.

In a randomized trial by Fowler and colleagues, high-dose daptomycin (6-10 mg/kg IV once daily) was non-inferior to standard therapy (vancomycin) for S. aureus bacteremia and right-sided endocarditis, serving as the primary bactericidal alternative for isolates with vancomycin MIC >1 mcg/mL.

Mandatory clinical management standards in MRSA bacteremia include repeat blood cultures at 48 to 72 hours until clearance is documented, echocardiography (transesophageal echocardiography preferred) to rule out infective endocarditis, and urgent source control (removal of infected intravascular catheters and surgical drainage of metastatic abscesses).

topic: MRSA: decolonisation, mupirocin, chlorhexidine, glycopeptides, daptomycin, linezolid

guidelinesKept: Clinical practice guidelines by the Infectious Diseases Society of America for the treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections in adults and children

page.mentor_intro: Hospital-associated MRSA transmission and invasive disease are mitigated by evidence-based infection control decolonization bundles and targeted systemic antimicrobial therapeutics, including glycopeptides, lipopeptides, and oxazolidinones tailored to site-specific pharmacokinetics.

teaching_points.claim: In the cluster-randomized REDUCE MRSA trial by Huang and colleagues evaluating 74,256 ICU patients, universal decolonization (daily chlorhexidine bathing plus twice-daily nasal mupirocin for all ICU patients) was significantly superior to targeted decolonization, reducing MRSA clinical isolates by 37% and all-cause bloodstream infections by 44%.

In non-ICU patients with medical devices, the cluster-randomized ABATE Infection trial demonstrated that daily chlorhexidine bathing and mupirocin decolonization significantly reduced clinical multidrug-resistant cultures and all-cause bloodstream infections by over 30%.

In hospital-acquired MRSA pneumonia, randomized trial evidence by Wunderink and colleagues showed that linezolid achieved higher clinical cure rates than vancomycin (57.6% vs 46.6%; p=0.042) due to superior penetration into pulmonary epithelial lining fluid.

Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) guidelines emphasize that daptomycin is strictly contraindicated in MRSA pneumonia because it is bound and inactivated by pulmonary surfactant, but is a first-line bactericidal agent for MRSA skin and soft-tissue infections and bacteremia.

page.mentor_intro: Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer represents an immunogenic tumor subtype characterized by dense neoantigen load, which responds dramatically to first-line immune checkpoint inhibition with pembrolizumab or nivolumab plus ipilimumab.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark phase 3 KEYNOTE-177 trial, first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy significantly doubled progression-free survival compared with standard chemotherapy (FOLFOX/FOLFIRI +/- bevacizumab or cetuximab) (median PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 months; HR 0.60; p=0.0002) in MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer.

Long-term 5-year updates of KEYNOTE-177 confirmed sustained durability: 5-year PFS was 34.0% with pembrolizumab versus 7.6% with chemotherapy, with significantly lower grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (22% vs 66%).

In the CheckMate 142 trial, dual immune checkpoint blockade with nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab as first-line therapy achieved an objective response rate of 69%, a disease control rate of 84%, and a 24-month progression-free survival rate of 74% in dMMR/MSI-H mCRC.

Mismatch repair deficiency causes a thousand-fold increase in replication error mutations, generating abundant frameshift-derived neoepitopes that stimulate dense tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, conferring susceptibility to PD-1/CTLA-4 axis blockade.

page.mentor_intro: The initial presentation of multiple sclerosis (MS) typically manifests as a clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) affecting the optic nerves, brainstem, or spinal cord in young adults, definitively diagnosed using the revised 2017 McDonald criteria requiring objective evidence of dissemination in space (DIS) and time (DIT).

teaching_points.claim: Under the revised 2017 McDonald criteria, dissemination in space (DIS) requires >=1 T2 hyperintense lesion in >=2 of 4 characteristic CNS areas: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord.

Dissemination in time (DIT) can be proven on a single baseline MRI by the simultaneous presence of asymptomatic gadolinium-enhancing and non-enhancing lesions, OR by the presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands, which now substitutes for DIT in patients fulfilling DIS criteria.

In the landmark Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial (ONTT), high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3 days) followed by oral prednisone accelerated visual recovery compared to placebo, whereas oral prednisone alone at standard doses paradoxically increased the rate of recurrent optic neuritis.

International guidelines recommend early initiation of high-efficacy or moderate-efficacy disease-modifying therapy (DMT) upon confirmation of relapsing MS to suppress subclinical inflammation, reduce relapse rates, and prevent long-term neurological disability.

topic: Multidrug-resistant TB: MDR, XDR definitions, bedaquiline, delamanid, novel regimens

guidelinesKept: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis: Module 4: Treatment - Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Treatment, 2022 Update

page.mentor_intro: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB, resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin) and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) represent major global health challenges, transformed by 6-month, all-oral, bedaquiline- and pretomanid-based therapeutic regimens.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized TB-PRACTECAL trial by Nyang'wa and colleagues, a 24-week, all-oral regimen of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin (BPaLM) achieved an 89% favorable outcome rate compared with 52% on standard care regimens, with significantly lower treatment discontinuations and serious adverse events.

The ZeNix randomized trial proved that the 6-month BPaL regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid) retained high treatment efficacy (89-93% favorable outcome) while lowering linezolid dosage from 1200 mg daily to 600 mg daily significantly reduced peripheral neuropathy (from 38% to 24%) and myelosuppression.

WHO 2022 consolidated guidelines recommend the 6-month all-oral BPaLM regimen (or BPaL if fluoroquinolone resistance is documented) as the preferred treatment for patients with MDR/RR-TB, replacing historical 18- to 24-month injectable regimens.

Under updated WHO definitions, extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB) is redefined as MDR/RR-TB that is also resistant to any fluoroquinolone AND at least one additional Group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid).

topic: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 MEN1: parathyroid, pituitary, pancreatic tumours

guidelinesKept: Clinical practice guidelines for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1)

page.mentor_intro: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1, Wermer syndrome) is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition syndrome caused by germline mutations in the MEN1 tumor suppressor gene encoding menin, classically manifesting with the '3 Ps': parathyroid adenomas/hyperplasia (>95%), enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (30-70%), and anterior pituitary adenomas (30-40%).

teaching_points.claim: Endocrine Society clinical guidelines state that primary hyperparathyroidism is the earliest and most common feature of MEN1, occurring in over 95% of patients by age 50, characterized by multiglandular parathyroid hyperplasia requiring subtotal (3.5-gland) parathyroidectomy or total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation.

Positional cloning established that MEN1 is caused by inactivating germline mutations in the MEN1 gene on chromosome 11q13, which encodes the 610-amino acid nuclear scaffold protein menin that interacts with transcription factors and histone methyltransferases.

In long-term prospective registry cohorts from the French GTE group, duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (especially gastrinomas causing Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and non-functioning pNETs) and thymic carcinoids represent the primary cause of disease-related mortality in MEN1.

Screening guidelines recommend annual biochemical surveillance (serum calcium, PTH, gastrin, chromogranin A, prolactin, IGF-1) starting in childhood (ages 5-10) and biennial pancreatic/pituitary imaging (contrast MRI or endoscopic ultrasound) for early neoplastic detection in mutation carriers.

topic: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 MEN2A and MEN2B: RET mutations, prophylactic thyroidectomy

guidelinesKept: Revised American Thyroid Association guidelines for the management of medullary thyroid carcinoma

page.mentor_intro: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2A and MEN2B) is caused by activating gain-of-function germline mutations in the RET proto-oncogene; clinical management relies on genotype-phenotype risk stratification to guide timely prophylactic total thyroidectomy and prevent fatal medullary thyroid carcinoma.

teaching_points.claim: According to the American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines, germline RET proto-oncogene mutations are categorized into risk tiers: Highest Risk (MEN2B, codon M918T) mandates prophylactic total thyroidectomy within the first year of life (first months if feasible).
High-risk mutations (classical MEN2A, codon C634) mandate prophylactic total thyroidectomy before age 5 years to prevent nodal metastases from medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC).

Pheochromocytoma develops in ~50% of patients with MEN2A and MEN2B (typically bilateral, benign); ATA guidelines mandate screening for pheochromocytoma (plasma free metanephrines) before neck surgery, and any identified pheochromocytoma must be resected first to avert intraoperative hypertensive crisis.

MEN2B is characterized clinically by the distinct syndromic triad of aggressive infancy-onset medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas (lips and tongue), intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (chronic constipation/megacolon), and a marfanoid habitus, lacking primary hyperparathyroidism.

page.mentor_intro: Multiple myeloma is a clonal plasma cell neoplasm producing monoclonal immunoglobulins and osteolytic bone destruction, diagnosed according to the revised International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) criteria encompassing traditional CRAB end-organ features and validated SLiM biomarkers of malignancy.

teaching_points.claim: The 2014 IMWG consensus criteria updated the diagnostic definition of multiple myeloma by adding three definitive 'SLiM' biomarkers that predict >=80% risk of progression to CRAB end-organ damage within 2 years: clonal bone marrow plasma cells >=60%, involved-to-uninvolved serum free light chain (FLC) ratio >=100, and >1 focal bone lesion (>=5 mm) on whole-body MRI.

Risk stratification is determined by the Revised International Staging System (R-ISS), integrating serum albumin, beta-2 microglobulin, serum LDH, and high-risk interphase fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) abnormalities: del(17p), t(4;14), and t(14;16).

IMWG consensus guidelines mandate low-dose whole-body CT (or whole-body MRI / 18F-FDG PET-CT) as first-line skeletal imaging, replacing conventional plain skeletal surveys due to superior sensitivity for detecting osteolytic lesions and marrow infiltration.

All symptomatic multiple myeloma patients require immediate supportive bone-targeted therapy with zoledronic acid or denosumab (denosumab preferred in patients with creatinine clearance <30 mL/min) to reduce skeletal-related events and pathologic fractures.

topic: Multiple myeloma: autologous stem cell transplantation

page.mentor_intro: High-dose melphalan conditioning followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) remains the established standard of care for transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, significantly prolonging progression-free survival and deepening minimal residual disease negativity.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark randomized IFM 2009 trial, early autologous stem cell transplantation following VRd induction significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with VRd chemotherapy alone (median PFS 50 vs 36 months; HR 0.65; p<0.001) and doubled the rate of complete response.

The DETERMINATION trial confirmed that early ASCT combined with continuous lenalidomide maintenance until disease progression extended median PFS to an unprecedented 67.5 months versus 46.2 months in the chemotherapy-only arm (HR 0.70; p<0.001).

In a meta-analysis of four randomized trials by McCarthy and colleagues, maintenance therapy with single-agent lenalidomide following ASCT significantly reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 52% and conferred a statistically significant 2.5-year improvement in overall survival.
Standard conditioning is high-dose intravenous melphalan (200 mg/m2), dose-reduced to 140 mg/m2 in patients with severe renal failure (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2) or advanced frailty.

page.mentor_intro: Incorporation of daratumumab (anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody) into frontline quadruplet induction regimens has redefined the standard of care for transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, achieving high minimal residual disease negativity rates and durable disease suppression.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 CASSIOPEIA trial, adding daratumumab to bortezomib, thalidomide, and dexamethasone (Dara-VTd) pre- and post-ASCT significantly increased stringent complete response rates (29% vs 20%; p=0.001) and reduced the risk of progression or death by 53% (HR 0.47; p<0.0001).

The randomized phase 2 GRIFFIN trial demonstrated that daratumumab plus VRd (Dara-VRd) followed by ASCT and Dara-R maintenance achieved high confirmed MRD negativity (<10^-5) of 64% versus 30% for VRd alone, with 4-year PFS of 87.2% vs 70.0%.

In the phase 3 PERSEUS trial, subcutaneous daratumumab combined with VRd induction and consolidation followed by daratumumab-lenalidomide maintenance significantly prolonged progression-free survival (48-month PFS 84.3% vs 67.7%; HR 0.42; p<0.001) and achieved 75.2% MRD negativity.

In transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, the landmark MAIA trial established that daratumumab plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd) significantly prolonged overall survival compared to Rd alone (5-year OS 66.3% vs 53.1%; HR 0.68; p=0.001).

page.mentor_intro: Daratumumab-based combination regimens span the entirety of the multiple myeloma therapeutic continuum, providing unprecedented response depth and overall survival prolongation in both newly diagnosed transplant-ineligible disease and relapsed/refractory settings.

teaching_points.claim: In transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, long-term follow-up of the phase 3 MAIA trial proved that daratumumab plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd) extended median progression-free survival beyond 5 years (61.9 vs 34.4 months; HR 0.53; p<0.0001) and significantly improved 5-year overall survival (66.3% vs 53.1%).

In the phase 3 ALCYONE trial, adding daratumumab to bortezomib, melphalan, and prednisone (Dara-VMP) in transplant-ineligible patients reduced the risk of death by 40% (HR 0.60; p=0.0003) and significantly increased minimal residual disease negativity (28% vs 7%).

In relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, the phase 3 POLLUX trial proved that Dara-Rd reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 63% (HR 0.37; p<0.001) compared with Rd alone, achieving unprecedented depth of response.

In the CASTOR trial for relapsed myeloma, daratumumab combined with bortezomib and dexamethasone (Dara-Vd) significantly extended progression-free survival (HR 0.39; p<0.001) compared with bortezomib-dexamethasone doublet therapy.

page.mentor_intro: Induction therapy in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma aims to achieve deep initial cytoreduction and maximal minimal residual disease negativity prior to high-dose melphalan consolidation, with contemporary quadruplet regimens outperforming historical triplets.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 GMMG-HD7 trial by Goldschmidt and colleagues, adding the anti-CD38 antibody isatuximab to VRd induction (Isa-VRd) significantly increased the rate of MRD negativity at the end of induction (50.1% vs 35.6%; OR 1.83; p<0.001) prior to autologous transplant.

In the randomized STaMINA trial, a single autologous stem cell transplant followed by lenalidomide maintenance demonstrated equivalent overall survival compared with tandem ASCT or post-transplant VRd consolidation, establishing single ASCT as the standard for standard-risk disease.

The randomized EMN02/HO95 trial confirmed that upfront ASCT significantly improved 5-year progression-free survival (53.5% vs 41.9%; HR 0.74; p=0.0001) and overall survival compared to intensified conventional chemotherapy (bortezomib, melphalan, and prednisone).
Induction regimens should avoid alkylating agents (e.g., oral melphalan) to prevent stem cell toxicity and preserve hematopoietic bone marrow stem cell collection reserves.

topic: Multiple myeloma: VRd versus Rd for newly diagnosed disease

page.mentor_intro: The triplet regimen of bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (VRd) established the superiority of proteasome inhibitor plus immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) combination therapy over doublet regimens for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, delivering significant progression-free and overall survival advantages.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark phase 3 SWOG S0777 trial by Durie and colleagues, newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients randomized to VRd experienced significantly longer progression-free survival (median 43 vs 30 months; HR 0.71; p=0.0018) and overall survival (median 75 vs 64 months; HR 0.71; p=0.025) compared to lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Rd) alone.

Long-term 7-year follow-up of SWOG S0777 confirmed that the survival benefit of adding bortezomib was sustained across both younger (<65 years) and older (>=65 years) cohorts, establishing triplet therapy as the standard baseline comparator.

The phase 3 FIRST trial demonstrated that continuous Rd until progression prolonged PFS compared with melphalan-prednisone-thalidomide (MPT), establishing continuous immunomodulation as a foundational backbone.
NCCN and international clinical practice guidelines designate VRd (or quadruplet Dara-VRd) as a preferred category 1 standard of care for initial therapy of multiple myeloma.

page.mentor_intro: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated chronic inflammatory and neurodegenerative disease of the central nervous system characterized by multifocal demyelination, astrocytic gliosis, and axonal transection, manifesting as relapsing-remitting or progressive disease requiring early diagnostic McDonald criteria verification and disease-modifying treatment.

teaching_points.claim: According to the revised 2017 McDonald criteria, diagnosis requires objective clinical and neuroimaging demonstration of lesions disseminated in space (DIS, involving >=2 of 4 typical CNS regions) and time (DIT, simultaneous contrast-enhancing and non-enhancing lesions or new lesions on follow-up).

The 2017 McDonald criteria established that the presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands (unique bands present in CSF but absent in matched serum) substitutes for the requirement of dissemination in time in patients with typical clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) fulfilling DIS criteria.

Clinical disease phenotype is standardized by the Lublin classification into clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS, ~85% of presentations), secondary progressive MS (SPMS), and primary progressive MS (PPMS, ~15%), each characterized by disease activity (clinical relapses or new MRI lesions) and progression.

ECTRIMS/EAN guidelines recommend starting disease-modifying therapy early in patients with CIS and abnormal baseline brain MRI showing >=2 demyelinating lesions, as early treatment significantly reduces conversion to clinically definite MS and delays long-term disability accumulation.

page.mentor_intro: Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) for multiple sclerosis have expanded into highly effective targeted immunomodulatory agents, including B-cell-depleting monoclonal antibodies, selective cell adhesion blockers, and oral pulsed immune reconstitution therapies that markedly reduce relapse rates and delay disability progression.

teaching_points.claim: In the twin OPERA I and OPERA II phase 3 trials, the humanized anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody ocrelizumab significantly reduced annualized relapse rates by 46-47% (p<0.001) and reduced 12-week confirmed disability progression by 40% compared with subcutaneous interferon beta-1a in relapsing MS.

In the phase 3 ORATORIO trial, ocrelizumab became the first disease-modifying therapy to demonstrate efficacy in primary progressive MS, significantly reducing 12-week confirmed disability progression by 24% (p=0.03) and decreasing total brain volume loss compared to placebo.

In the AFFIRM trial, the alpha-4 integrin antagonist natalizumab reduced annualized relapse rates by 68% (p<0.001) and reduced sustained disability progression by 42%, though long-term therapy mandates strict anti-JCV antibody index surveillance to stratify progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) risk.

ECTRIMS/EAN consensus guidelines support early use of high-efficacy DMTs (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, natalizumab, alemtuzumab) in patients with highly active disease (frequent disabling relapses or multiple spinal/infratentorial gadolinium-enhancing lesions).

topic: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA): MSA-P vs MSA-C, autonomic failure profiling
