page.mentor_intro: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is an adult-onset, fatal, rapidly progressive neurodegenerative alpha-synucleinopathy characterized by prominent autonomic failure combined with either poorly levodopa-responsive parkinsonism (MSA-P) or cerebellar ataxia (MSA-C).

teaching_points.claim: According to the 2022 Movement Disorder Society (MDS) consensus criteria, clinically established MSA requires adult onset (>=30 years), progressive disease course, and severe autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension >=30 mmHg systolic or >=15 mmHg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing, or neurogenic urinary incontinence / incomplete bladder emptying), accompanied by poorly levodopa-responsive parkinsonism or cerebellar syndrome.

MSA is categorized by dominant motor presentation: MSA-P (predominant parkinsonian features, prominent in Western populations) and MSA-C (predominant cerebellar ataxia, prominent in Japanese cohorts).

Pathognomonic neuroimaging markers on brain MRI include the 'hot-cross-bun' sign (T2 hyperintensity cruciform pattern in the pons from degeneration of pontocerebellar fibers) and the 'putaminal rim sign' (linear T2 hypointensity with lateral hyperintense margin).

Autonomic profiling demonstrates severe pre-ganglionic sympathetic and parasympathetic degeneration, leading to profound postprandial hypotension, nocturnal supine hypertension, and sleep-related laryngeal stridor (a life-threatening feature that warrants continuous positive airway pressure or tracheostomy).

page.mentor_intro: Musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSUS) provides real-time, non-invasive bedside assessment of synovial proliferation, tenosynovitis, and enthesitis; power Doppler (PD) imaging detects active synovial hypervascularity to monitor therapeutic response and guide precise intra-articular interventions.

teaching_points.claim: OMERACT ultrasound consensus definitions establish standardized criteria for synovial hypertrophy, joint effusion, tenosynovitis, and bone erosion, utilizing semi-quantitative grading (grades 0-3) for both grayscale B-mode and power Doppler vascularity.

Power Doppler ultrasound detects low-velocity microvascular blood flow within thickened synovial tissue; persistence of PD signals in patients with rheumatoid arthritis in clinical remission predicts ongoing joint damage progression and imminent disease flare.

In a randomized controlled trial by Sibbitt and colleagues, ultrasound-guided intra-articular injections significantly reduced procedural pain by 43%, increased successful synovial aspiration from 68% to 100%, and achieved significantly greater and more prolonged clinical response compared to anatomic landmark-guided palpation.

EULAR recommendations endorse musculoskeletal ultrasound for early confirmation of synovitis in patients with clinically equivocal joint swelling, establishing inflammatory arthritis diagnosis weeks to months earlier than clinical examination alone.

page.mentor_intro: Targeted immunotherapies for generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) have revolutionized management of acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive disease through selective terminal complement C5 inhibition (eculizumab, ravulizumab) and neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blockade (efgartigimod), inducing rapid functional improvement in refractory disease.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized phase 3 REGAIN trial by Howard and colleagues, the terminal complement C5 inhibitor eculizumab produced significant, clinically meaningful, and sustained improvements in Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) and QMG scores in refractory anti-AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis.

In the phase 3 ADAPT trial, the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) antagonist efgartigimod achieved rapid reductions in total IgG and anti-AChR antibody titers, producing significant, durable MG-ADL responder rates (67.7% vs 29.7% with placebo; p<0.0001) in generalized myasthenia gravis.

The phase 3 CHAMPION-MG trial demonstrated that the long-acting terminal complement C5 inhibitor ravulizumab produced rapid and sustained improvements in MG-ADL scores through week 26 with convenient 8-weekly maintenance dosing.

International consensus guidance mandates that all patients receiving terminal complement inhibitors (eculizumab, ravulizumab) must receive meningococcal vaccination (serogroups A, C, W, Y and B) at least 2 weeks prior to therapy and prophylactic oral antibiotics until immunization takes effect, due to an increased risk of invasive Neisseria meningitidis infection.

page.mentor_intro: Mycobacterial and fungal arthritis are chronic, indolent joint infections presenting as slowly progressive monoarticular arthritis, characteristically causing substantial diagnostic delay and requiring synovial tissue histopathology, acid-fast and fungal staining, mycobacterial culture/PCR, and prolonged targeted antimicrobial therapy combined with surgical debridement.

teaching_points.claim: Tuberculous arthritis typically presents as an indolent, insidious, chronic monoarthritis (most commonly affecting weight-bearing joints: knee, hip, ankle) or spondylodiscitis (Pott's disease); synovial fluid smears are positive for acid-fast bacilli in <30% of cases, making synovial biopsy with granuloma identification and mycobacterial culture/PCR the diagnostic gold standard.

ATS/CDC/IDSA clinical guidelines recommend treating musculoskeletal and joint tuberculosis with standard four-drug therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) for 2 months followed by rifampicin and isoniazid for a total duration of 6 to 9 months.

In Candida arthritis, IDSA guidelines mandate surgical debridement or drainage combined with systemic antifungal therapy: fluconazole (400 mg daily) or an echinocandin (caspofungin/anidulafungin) for at least 6 weeks; prosthetic joint involvement necessitates two-stage revision arthroplasty.

Endemic fungal joint infections (Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Histoplasma, Sporothrix schenckii) occur via hematogenous dissemination or direct occupational inoculation (e.g., rose thorn prick causing sporotrichoid lymphocutaneous arthritis), treated with intravenous amphotericin B followed by prolonged oral itraconazole for 6-12 months.

page.mentor_intro: In proliferative lupus nephritis (ISN/RPS Class III/IV), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) and intravenous cyclophosphamide achieve comparable remission induction efficacy, with MMF demonstrating superior tolerability, higher response rates in non-Caucasian populations, and established superiority as maintenance therapy.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark Aspreva Lupus Management Study (ALMS) induction trial by Appel and colleagues, mycophenolate mofetil (target 3 g daily) demonstrated equivalent overall renal remission rates to intravenous pulse cyclophosphamide (56.2% vs 53.0%), while showing superior response rates in Black and Hispanic patients.

In the ALMS maintenance trial, Dooley and colleagues proved that MMF was significantly superior to azathioprine in maintaining renal remission (treatment failure rate 16.4% vs 32.4%; HR 0.44; p=0.003) and significantly prolonged time to renal flare over 36 months.

The Euro-Lupus Nephritis Trial established that a low-dose intravenous cyclophosphamide induction regimen (six fortnightly pulses of 500 mg, cumulative dose 3 g) followed by azathioprine achieved long-term renal remission, renal function preservation, and 10-year survival equivalent to high-dose cyclical cyclophosphamide.

EULAR/ERA-EDTA guidelines recommend MMF or low-dose Euro-Lupus intravenous cyclophosphamide combined with glucocorticoids as preferred first-line induction for Class III/IV lupus nephritis, with cyclophosphamide preferred in patients with rapidly declining renal function or nephrotic-range proteinuria failing oral therapy.

page.mentor_intro: Mycosis fungoides (MF) and Sézary syndrome (SS) are cutaneous T-cell lymphomas (CTCL) of skin-homing CD4+ memory T lymphocytes; management is stage-adapted, employing skin-directed therapies (topical corticosteroids, nitrogen mustard, phototherapy) for early-stage disease and targeted systemic therapies (brentuximab vedotin, mogamulizumab) for advanced disease.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized phase 3 ALCANZA trial, the CD30-directed antibody-drug conjugate brentuximab vedotin demonstrated significant superiority over physician's choice (methotrexate or bexarotene) in CD30-positive cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, achieving an objective response lasting >=4 months (ORR4) of 56.3% versus 12.5% (p<0.0001).

The phase 3 MAVORIC trial showed that mogamulizumab (monoclonal antibody targeting CC chemokine receptor 4, CCR4) significantly doubled median progression-free survival compared to vorinostat (7.7 vs 3.1 months; HR 0.53; p<0.0001), demonstrating particularly high activity in the blood compartment of Sézary syndrome.

The ISCL/EORTC staging system classifies MF and SS by TNMB criteria, defining Sézary syndrome as leukemic CTCL characterized by generalized erythroderma (T4) and significant peripheral blood involvement (B2: absolute Sézary cell count >=1.0 x 10^9/L, CD4/CD8 ratio >=10, or loss of CD7/CD26 on CD4+ cells).

EORTC and WHO guidelines establish that early-stage disease (Stage IA-IIA: patches and plaques covering <10% to >=10% body surface area without tumors) is managed conservatively with skin-directed therapies (topical corticosteroids, topical chlormethine/mechlorethamine gel, PUVA or narrow-band UVB phototherapy) to avoid unnecessary systemic chemotherapy toxicity.

page.mentor_intro: Azacitidine is a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor that represents the established standard-of-care hypomethylating therapy for higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), demonstrating proven overall survival prolongation and delayed progression to acute myeloid leukemia.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark randomized phase 3 AZA-001 trial by Fenaux and colleagues, azacitidine (75 mg/m2/day subcutaneously for 7 consecutive days every 28 days) significantly prolonged median overall survival from 15.0 months with conventional care to 24.5 months (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.43-0.77; p=0.0001) in higher-risk MDS.

In AZA-001, azacitidine almost doubled the 2-year overall survival rate compared to conventional care regimens (50.8% vs 26.2%; p<0.0001) and significantly delayed the median time to acute myeloid leukemia transformation from 11.5 to 17.8 months.

Risk stratification is guided by the Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R), incorporating cytogenetic risk categories, marrow blast percentage, depth of cytopenias, and age; higher-risk categories (intermediate, high, very high) are standard indications for hypomethylating therapy.

European LeukemiaNet (ELN) guidelines emphasize that a minimum of 4 to 6 cycles of azacitidine must be administered before evaluating for clinical response or declaring treatment failure, as responses develop gradually over multiple treatment cycles.

page.mentor_intro: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) encompass a heterogeneous spectrum of clonal hematopoietic stem cell neoplasms characterized by peripheral cytopenias, ineffective hematopoiesis, and risk of acute myeloid leukemia transformation, managed by genomic risk-stratified therapy.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 MEDALIST trial by Fenaux and colleagues, the erythroid maturation agent luspatercept (1.0-1.75 mg/kg subcutaneously every 3 weeks) significantly reduced transfusion burden in lower-risk MDS with ring sideroblasts, achieving transfusion independence for >=8 weeks in 38% vs 13% with placebo (p<0.001).

In patients with lower-risk MDS and isolated del(5q) cytogenetic abnormality, lenalidomide produces rapid and durable transfusion independence in 67% of patients and complete cytogenetic remission in 45% by targeting casein kinase 1A1 (CK1A1) for ubiquitination and degradation.

Prognostication has advanced from the Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R) to the Molecular IPSS (IPSS-M), which incorporates targeted next-generation sequencing across 31 genes, identifying multi-hit TP53, SF3B1, and ASXL1 as critical independent molecular risk modifiers.

For symptomatic lower-risk non-del(5q) MDS with serum erythropoietin <500 U/L and low transfusion burden, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (recombinant human EPO or darbepoetin alfa) achieve an erythroid hematologic response in 40-60% of patients.

page.mentor_intro: Myelofibrosis is a BCR-ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasm driven by dysregulated JAK-STAT signaling, causing debilitating constitutional symptoms, progressive extramedullary hematopoiesis with massive splenomegaly, and bone marrow reticulin fibrosis, effectively palliated by the oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib.

teaching_points.claim: In the double-blind, randomized COMFORT-I trial, ruxolitinib significantly reduced splenomegaly in primary or secondary myelofibrosis, with 41.9% of patients achieving >=35% spleen volume reduction at 24 weeks compared to 0.7% with placebo (p<0.001), accompanied by dramatic improvements in disease-related constitutional symptoms.

The randomized COMFORT-II trial confirmed ruxolitinib superiority over best available therapy (28% vs 0% achieving >=35% spleen volume reduction at week 48; p<0.001) and established significant quality-of-life and functional capacity improvements.

Pooled 5-year long-term survival analyses of COMFORT-I and COMFORT-II demonstrated that ruxolitinib conferred a statistically significant 30% reduction in the risk of all-cause death (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.54-0.91; p=0.0065) compared with control cohorts.

Ruxolitinib dosing is titrated based on baseline platelet count (20 mg twice daily for platelets >200 x 10^9/L, 15 mg twice daily for 100-200 x 10^9/L, 5 mg twice daily for 50-100 x 10^9/L); early dose-dependent anemia and thrombocytopenia represent expected mechanism-based pharmacodynamic effects rather than drug toxicity.

page.mentor_intro: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is defined by the Fourth Universal Definition as cardiomyocyte necrosis in a clinical setting consistent with acute myocardial ischemia, mandating rapid differentiation between atherothrombotic plaque disruption (Type 1 MI) and supply-demand mismatch (Type 2 MI) using high-sensitivity cardiac troponin algorithms.

teaching_points.claim: The Fourth Universal Definition of MI distinguishes Type 1 MI (coronary atherothrombosis caused by plaque rupture, ulceration, or erosion) from Type 2 MI (ischemic myocardial injury resulting from a mismatch between oxygen supply and demand without acute atherothrombosis, such as sustained tachyarrhythmia, severe anemia, or shock).

ESC guidelines recommend the rapid 0h/1h or 0h/2h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) algorithmic protocols, which achieve negative predictive values >99% for safe early discharge in the rule-out zone while rapidly identifying high-risk patients in the rule-in zone.

In ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), emergency primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) is the Class I reperfusion strategy of choice if the anticipated time from STEMI diagnosis to wire crossing is <=120 minutes; otherwise, immediate intravenous fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of diagnosis is mandated.

Acute secondary prevention mandates immediate loading of dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin plus a potent P2Y12 inhibitor: ticagrelor or prasugrel preferred over clopidogrel), high-intensity statin therapy (atorvastatin 80 mg), and beta-blocker/ACE inhibitor initiation within 24 hours in the absence of cardiogenic shock.

topic: Myoclonus: classification (cortical vs subcortical), pharmacological approaches

page.mentor_intro: Myoclonus consists of sudden, brief, shock-like involuntary muscle contractions (positive myoclonus) or lapses of muscle tone (negative myoclonus/asterixis), categorized by anatomical origin into cortical, subcortical, spinal, and peripheral forms to guide neurophysiological evaluation and targeted pharmacotherapy.

teaching_points.claim: Neurophysiological testing differentiates cortical from subcortical myoclonus: cortical myoclonus features extremely brief EMG bursts (<50 ms), giant somatosensory evoked potentials (P25/N33 amplitude >10 mcV), enhanced long-latency transcortical C-reflex, and pre-movement cortical potentials on jerk-locked back-averaging.

Pharmacological therapy for cortical myoclonus prioritizes broad-spectrum GABAergic and anti-seizure medications: levetiracetam (1000-3000 mg/day), clonazepam (2-8 mg/day), and sodium valproate (1000-2000 mg/day) represent first-line evidence-based treatments.

Subcortical myoclonus (including reticular reflex myoclonus and propriospinal myoclonus) originates in the brainstem or spinal cord with EMG burst durations typically 50-200 ms, absent giant SSEPs, and preferential clinical responsiveness to clonazepam.

Clinicians must avoid sodium channel-blocking antiepileptic drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine) in progressive myoclonus epilepsies (such as Unverricht-Lundborg disease), as they can paradoxically exacerbate cortical myoclonic jerks and ataxia.

topic: Myositis-specific antibodies: anti-Jo-1, anti-MDA5, anti-TIF1-gamma: clinical associations

guidelinesKept: 2017 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for adult and juvenile idiopathic inflammatory myopathies

page.mentor_intro: Myositis-specific autoantibodies (MSAs) delineate biologically and clinically distinct subsets of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, predicting distinct patterns of organ involvement, rapid interstitial lung disease progression, and occult malignancy risk.

teaching_points.claim: According to EULAR/ACR guidelines and international consensus, myositis-specific antibodies are mutually exclusive in over 95% of patients and define clinical phenotypes: anti-synthetase syndrome (anti-Jo-1, anti-PL-7, anti-PL-12), clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive ILD (anti-MDA5), cancer-associated dermatomyositis (anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-NXP2), and immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (anti-SRP, anti-HMGCR).

Anti-MDA5 antibodies (melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5) are strongly associated with clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis, characterized by palmar/digital cuticular ulcers, painful violaceous papules, and hyper-acute rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RPILD) carrying mortality >50% within 6 months.

In a systematic review and meta-analysis by Trallero-Araguas and colleagues, anti-TIF1-gamma (tripartite motif-containing 33) and anti-NXP2 antibodies in adult dermatomyositis were associated with a dramatic increase in concurrent malignancy (pooled sensitivity 78%, specificity 89%; OR 27.2 for cancer-associated myositis), necessitating comprehensive age-appropriate whole-body cancer screening.

The anti-synthetase syndrome (most commonly anti-Jo-1, targeting histidyl-tRNA synthetase) presents with the classical pentad of non-erosive inflammatory arthritis, myositis, interstitial lung disease, Raynaud's phenomenon, and hyperkeratotic 'mechanic's hands'.

topic: Myotonic Dystrophy (Type 1 and 2): CTG/CCTG repeats, systemic complications

page.mentor_intro: Myotonic dystrophy is an autosomal dominant multisystem disorder characterized by myotonia, progressive skeletal muscle weakness, cardiac conduction defects, premature cataracts, and endocrine disturbances, caused by non-coding unstable microsatellite repeat expansions in DMPK (Type 1) or CNBP (Type 2).

teaching_points.claim: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1, Steinert disease) is caused by an unstable CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the 3' untranslated region of the DMPK gene on chromosome 19q13.3; normal alleles have 5-34 repeats, whereas affected individuals harbor 50 to thousands of repeats, demonstrating genetic anticipation with earlier and more severe onset across generations.

Myotonic dystrophy type 2 (DM2, PROMM) is caused by an unstable CCTG tetranucleotide repeat expansion in intron 1 of the CNBP (ZNF9) gene on chromosome 3q21.3; unlike DM1, DM2 features proximal rather than distal muscle weakness, lacks a severe congenital form, and does not show significant genetic anticipation.

In a prospective registry study by Wahbi and colleagues evaluating 914 DM1 patients, baseline PR interval prolongation >=240 ms, QRS duration >=120 ms, and advanced atrioventricular block on annual ECG independently predicted sudden cardiac death, establishing clear indications for invasive electrophysiological studies and prophylactic pacemaker/ICD implantation.

Systemic complications require structured multidisciplinary surveillance: annual 12-lead ECG and Holter monitoring, sleep studies for obstructive/central sleep apnea, slit-lamp examination for pathognomonic iridescent posterior capsular cataracts, and pulmonary function testing (forced vital capacity) to detect diaphragmatic weakness.

topic: Narrow-complex tachycardias: SVT diagnosis, vagal manoeuvres, adenosine, ablation

guidelinesKept: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the management of patients with supraventricular tachycardia
2015 ACC/AHA/HRS Guideline for the Management of Adult Patients With Supraventricular Tachycardia

page.mentor_intro: Narrow-complex tachycardia (QRS <120 ms) is a common medical emergency requiring urgent hemodynamic assessment, diagnostic 12-lead ECG appraisal of P-wave and RP relationships, physical vagal maneuvers, intravenous adenosine, and consideration of curative catheter ablation.

teaching_points.claim: In the multicenter randomized REVERT trial by Appelboam and colleagues, the modified postural Valsalva manoeuvre (straining to 40 mmHg for 15 seconds followed immediately by supine repositioning with 45-degree passive leg elevation for 15 seconds) achieved 43% cardioversion of SVT to sinus rhythm compared with only 17% for standard Valsalva (OR 3.7; NNT 3.8).

ESC and ACC/AHA guidelines establish intravenous adenosine (6 mg rapid IV push through large proximal vein with saline flush, followed by 12 mg if unsuccessful) as the drug of choice for acute termination of paroxysmal SVT dependent on the AV node (AVNRT and AVRT).

Diagnostic ECG analysis categorizes regular narrow-complex tachycardias into short RP tachycardias (RP < PR interval, including typical slow-fast AVNRT and orthodromic AVRT) and long RP tachycardias (RP > PR interval, including atypical fast-slow AVNRT, permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia [PJRT], and atrial tachycardia).

Catheter ablation is the Class I definitive curative standard of care for recurrent symptomatic AVNRT and AVRT, achieving long-term success rates >97% with an exceedingly low risk of accidental permanent complete heart block (<1%).

page.mentor_intro: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH, formerly NASH) is the progressive inflammatory and fibrosing subtype of metabolic liver disease, leading to cirrhosis, hepatic failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma, managed by lifestyle-induced weight loss, liver-directed pharmacotherapies (resmetirom), and incretin-based metabolic therapies.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark phase 3 MAJESTY/Resmetirom trial by Harrison and colleagues, the liver-directed, oral thyroid hormone receptor-beta (THR-beta) selective agonist resmetirom (80 mg and 100 mg daily) achieved MASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis in 29.9% of patients (vs 9.7% with placebo; p<0.001) and achieved fibrosis improvement by >=1 stage in 25.9% (vs 14.2% with placebo; p<0.001).

In a randomized trial by Newsome and colleagues, once-daily subcutaneous semaglutide (0.4 mg) produced histological resolution of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis without worsening of fibrosis in 59% of patients compared with 17% in the placebo group (p<0.001).

AASLD practice guidance recommends non-invasive risk stratification for significant fibrosis (>=F2) using the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (combining age, AST, ALT, and platelets); scores <1.3 exclude advanced fibrosis, whereas scores >2.67 warrant immediate secondary testing with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE / FibroScan liver stiffness >=8.0 kPa) or hepatology referral.

Histopathological diagnosis and severity grading utilize the NAFLD Activity Score (NAS), which aggregates steatosis (0-3), lobular inflammation (0-3), and hepatocellular ballooning (0-2); hepatocellular ballooning is the pathognomonic histological hallmark distinguishing active steatohepatitis from simple steatosis.

page.mentor_intro: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an epithelial malignancy of the nasopharynx etiologically linked to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in endemic regions, characterized by early cervical lymphatic dissemination, monitored by plasma circulating EBV DNA, and treated with gemcitabine-cisplatin chemotherapy, concurrent chemoradiotherapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitors.

teaching_points.claim: In the phase 3 JUPITER-02 trial by Mai and colleagues, adding the anti-PD-1 antibody toripalimab to first-line gemcitabine and cisplatin in recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma significantly prolonged progression-free survival (median PFS 11.7 vs 8.0 months; HR 0.52; p=0.0003) and significantly improved overall survival.

The phase 3 CAPTAIN-1st trial demonstrated that camrelizumab combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin significantly prolonged progression-free survival (median 9.7 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.54; p=0.0002) in recurrent or metastatic NPC, confirming PD-1 blockade as standard frontline systemic therapy.

In locally advanced non-metastatic NPC, a landmark phase 3 trial by Zhang and colleagues showed that adding induction chemotherapy with gemcitabine plus cisplatin to concurrent chemoradiotherapy significantly improved 3-year overall survival (94.6% vs 90.3%; HR 0.43; p=0.02) and recurrence-free survival.

ESMO guidelines establish quantitative plasma circulating cell-free EBV DNA (cfEBV DNA) as the primary biomarker for clinical staging, post-treatment response assessment, and sensitive longitudinal surveillance for subclinical distant relapse.

topic: Necrotising fasciitis: diagnosis, LRINEC score, surgical debridement, polymicrobial coverage
cluster: Emergency Medicine / General Surgery / Critical Care

guidelinesKept: Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections: 2014 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America

page.mentor_intro: Necrotising fasciitis is a rapidly progressive, limb- and life-threatening subcutaneous and fascial infection characterized by extensive tissue necrosis, systemic toxicity, and gas production; emergent, radical surgical debridement is the cornerstone of survival, supported by broad-spectrum bactericidal antimicrobial and antitoxin therapy.

teaching_points.claim: In a diagnostic meta-analysis by Fernando and colleagues, the LRINEC (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis) score demonstrated a sensitivity of only 68.2%, meaning over 30% of surgical emergencies would be missed if a low LRINEC score (<6) was used to exclude necrotizing soft-tissue infection.

Survival is governed fundamentally by time to first operating room intervention; observational data by Bilton and colleagues showed that operative debridement within 12-24 hours of admission significantly reduces mortality compared to delayed intervention (>24 hours), which more than doubles surgical mortality.

IDSA guidelines mandate immediate empirical antimicrobial therapy covering polymicrobial Type I necrotizing fasciitis (mixed aerobes and anaerobes) and monomicrobial Type II (Group A Streptococcus or MRSA): vancomycin or daptomycin, PLUS piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem, PLUS clindamycin for ribosomal suppression of streptococcal and staphylococcal pyrogenic exotoxins.

Classical early physical examination findings are deceptive: severe, excruciating pain disproportionate to visible physical cutaneous findings, woody induration of subcutaneous tissues beyond visible erythema, and rapid centrifugal progression.

topic: Neonatal jaundice: assessment, phototherapy and exchange transfusion

guidelinesKept: Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinemia in the Newborn Infant 35 or More Weeks of Gestation

page.mentor_intro: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia affects over 60% of term and 80% of preterm infants; systematic predischarge risk assessment using transcutaneous bilirubinometry and total serum bilirubin mapped against hour-specific nomograms prevents acute bilirubin encephalopathy and irreversible kernicterus.

teaching_points.claim: The revised 2022 American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) clinical practice guideline updates hour-specific phototherapy and exchange transfusion thresholds, recommending universal predischarge transcutaneous bilirubin (TcB) or total serum bilirubin (TSB) measurement between 24 and 48 hours of life or prior to discharge.

Bhutani and colleagues proved that plotting predischarge hour-specific bilirubin on a percentile nomogram accurately stratifies infants into risk zones (high risk >95th percentile, high intermediate, low intermediate, and low risk <40th percentile), predicting significant hyperbilirubinemia requiring readmission.

Unconjugated bilirubin crosses the blood-brain barrier when binding capacity of albumin is exceeded or in neurovascular disruption, selectively depositing in the basal ganglia (globus pallidus), subthalamic nuclei, and brainstem auditory nuclei, causing acute bilirubin encephalopathy (lethargy, hypotonia, high-pitched cry, retrocollis/opisthotonus) and chronic choreoathetoid kernicterus.

Intensive phototherapy utilizing narrow-band blue light (wavelength 460-490 nm) converts hydrophobic unconjugated bilirubin into water-soluble structural photoisomers (primarily lumirubin) that are excreted directly into bile and urine without requiring hepatic glucuronidation.

topic: Neonatal Lupus and Congenital Heart Block

guidelinesKept: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Reproductive Health in Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Diseases

page.mentor_intro: Neonatal lupus erythematosus is an acquired autoimmune disease mediated by transplacental transfer of maternal anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB autoantibodies, causing irreversible congenital heart block (CHB) in 2% of primigravida pregnancies and carrying high fetal morbidity and pacemaker dependence.

teaching_points.claim: In the prospective PRIDE study by Buyon and colleagues, transplacental transfer of maternal IgG anti-Ro/SSA (specifically anti-Ro52) and anti-La/SSB antibodies between 16 and 26 weeks gestation induced autoimmune inflammatory injury and fibrosis of the fetal atrioventricular node and conduction tissue.

Once third-degree (complete) congenital heart block develops, it is permanent and irreversible; over 80% of affected surviving children require permanent ventricular pacemaker implantation in infancy or early childhood.

ACR reproductive health guidelines recommend serial fetal echocardiography every 1 to 2 weeks from 16 to 26 weeks of gestation in all anti-Ro/SSA-positive pregnant women to detect early first- or second-degree heart block or endocardial fibroelastosis.

Non-cardiac manifestations of neonatal lupus (erythematous annular skin lesions, thrombocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, transaminitis) are benign and completely self-limited, spontaneously resolving by 6 to 8 months of age as maternal IgG autoantibodies are cleared from the infant's circulation.

topic: Neonatal lupus: anti-Ro, anti-La, congenital heart block, counselling

page.mentor_intro: Pre-conception and antenatal counseling for anti-Ro and anti-La antibody-positive women requires precise recurrence risk quantification and proactive secondary prevention with hydroxychloroquine to reduce recurrent congenital heart block.

teaching_points.claim: In the prospective, multicenter PATCH trial by Izmirly and colleagues, maternal treatment with oral hydroxychloroquine (400 mg daily) initiated before 10 weeks of gestation significantly reduced the recurrence rate of congenital heart block in women with a previously affected child from historical 18% down to 7.4% (p=0.002).

During pre-pregnancy counseling, clinicians must communicate exact baseline risks: the risk of congenital heart block in an anti-Ro-positive woman with no prior affected child is approximately 2%, whereas the recurrence risk in a subsequent pregnancy following an affected child rises tenfold to 18-20%.

ACR reproductive guidelines recommend that all anti-Ro/SSA-positive women continue or initiate hydroxychloroquine throughout pregnancy and undergo serial fetal echocardiography monitoring mechanical PR intervals every 1 to 2 weeks from 16 to 26 weeks gestation.

Cutaneous neonatal lupus manifests as annular, erythematous polycyclic plaques with central clearing in sun-exposed areas (particularly the periorbital 'raccoon-eyes' distribution), which resolves completely without scarring as maternal IgG clears by 6 months of age.

page.mentor_intro: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI) results from renal collecting duct unresponsiveness to arginine vasopressin (AVP), producing massive polyuria (>3 L/24h), polydipsia, and hyposthenuria, caused congenitally by AVPR2 or AQP2 mutations or acquired through chronic lithium therapy.

teaching_points.claim: Congenital NDI is caused in ~90% of cases by X-linked recessive loss-of-function mutations in the arginine vasopressin type 2 receptor gene (AVPR2 on chromosome Xq28), and in ~10% by autosomal recessive or dominant mutations in the aquaporin-2 water channel gene (AQP2 on chromosome 12q13).

Chronic lithium therapy is the most common cause of acquired NDI, occurring in up to 20-40% of patients; lithium enters principal cells through the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) and accumulates intracellularly, inhibiting glycogen synthase kinase-3beta (GSK-3beta) and downregulating AQP2 gene expression.

In diagnostic trials by Fenske and colleagues, plasma copeptin (the C-terminal cleavage fragment of pre-pro-vasopressin) measurement provides high accuracy: baseline un-stimulated copeptin >21.4 pmol/L confirms nephrogenic diabetes insipidus without requiring water deprivation.

Pharmacological management combines a low-sodium low-protein diet with a thiazide diuretic (which contracts extracellular fluid volume, increasing proximal tubular sodium and water reabsorption) and amiloride (which specifically blocks ENaC, preventing further lithium uptake in principal cells).

page.mentor_intro: Calcium nephrolithiasis (calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate) accounts for >80% of urinary calculi; recurrence prevention is guided by 24-hour urine metabolic profiling, dietary calcium normalization, and targeted pharmacological therapies (thiazides, potassium citrate).

teaching_points.claim: In a landmark 5-year randomized trial by Borghi and colleagues, a diet with normal calcium (1200 mg daily), low animal protein, and low sodium significantly reduced 5-year stone recurrence by 51% (relative risk 0.49; p=0.04) compared with a low-calcium diet (400 mg daily), because dietary calcium binds intestinal oxalate and reduces urinary oxalate excretion.

AUA and EAU guidelines mandate 24-hour urine metabolic evaluation in high-risk or recurrent stone formers, assessing urine volume, calcium, oxalate, citrate, uric acid, sodium, potassium, and pH to direct personalized medical prevention.

Thiazide diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide 25-50 mg daily, chlorthalidone 25-50 mg daily, indapamide 2.5 mg daily) stimulate renal proximal and distal tubular calcium reabsorption, significantly reducing 24-hour urinary calcium excretion and recurrent stone episodes.

Potassium citrate supplementation (30-60 mEq daily) is the primary therapy for hypocitraturia (<320 mg/day), providing alkali to increase urinary citrate excretion (a potent endogenous inhibitor of calcium stone crystallization) and alkalinize urine.

topic: Nephrolithiasis: Uric Acid and Struvite Stones

guidelinesKept: Medical management of kidney stones: AUA guideline
EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis

page.mentor_intro: Non-calcium urinary calculi include radiolucent uric acid stones driven by persistent acidic urine and infectious struvite staghorn calculi driven by urease-producing bacteria, requiring distinct diagnostic strategies, targeted urinary alkalinization, and surgical eradication.

teaching_points.claim: Uric acid nephrolithiasis is primarily driven by persistently acidic urinary pH (<5.5) rather than absolute hyperuricosuria; oral chemolysis with potassium citrate targeting urinary pH 6.5 to 7.0 successfully dissolves existing calculi and prevents recurrence.

Struvite (triple phosphate: magnesium ammonium phosphate and carbonate apatite) stones develop in the setting of chronic upper urinary tract infection with urease-producing organisms (Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella, Providencia, Pseudomonas), which hydrolyze urea into carbon dioxide and ammonia, driving alkaline urine pH (>7.2).

EAU and AUA guidelines mandate complete surgical clearance (percutaneous nephrolithotomy [PCNL] preferred) for struvite staghorn stones, as residual fragments harbor viable bacteria within the stone matrix that inevitably perpetuate recurrent sepsis and progressive renal destruction.

Uric acid stones are characteristically radiolucent on conventional plain radiography (KUB) but readily identified as high-attenuation calculi (200-400 Hounsfield units) on non-contrast computed tomography, distinguished from calcium stones (>800 HU).

guidelinesKept: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Glomerular Diseases

page.mentor_intro: Nephrotic syndrome is a clinical and biochemical syndrome defined by heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/24h or urine protein-to-creatinine ratio >350 mg/mmol), hypoalbuminemia (<30 g/L), peripheral edema, and hyperlipidemia, demanding systematic evaluation to distinguish primary podocytopathies from systemic disease.

teaching_points.claim: The diagnostic definition requires the complete nephrotic triad: heavy proteinuria exceeding 3.5 g per 24 hours (or spot urine protein:creatinine ratio >3000-3500 mg/g), profound hypoalbuminemia (<30 g/L), and peripheral edema, universally accompanied by dyslipidemia.

In adults, membranous nephropathy, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), and minimal change disease account for >80% of primary cases; serological testing for anti-PLA2R antibodies identifies primary membranous nephropathy with >95% specificity, frequently eliminating the requirement for renal biopsy.

Profound hypercoagulability results from urinary loss of endogenous anticoagulants (antithrombin III, protein S) and hepatic synthesis of procoagulant fibrinogen; in membranous nephropathy with severe hypoalbuminemia (serum albumin <28 g/L), prophylactic anticoagulation is indicated to prevent deep vein thrombosis and renal vein thrombosis.

KDIGO guidelines emphasize supportive management across all etiologies: loop diuretics combined with thiazides for edema, maximally tolerated ACE inhibitors or ARBs combined with SGLT2 inhibitors for antiproteinuric renoprotection, and statin therapy for severe dyslipidemia.

topic: Neurocritical care: management of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage

guidelinesKept: 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
Critical care management of patients following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: recommendations from the Neurocritical Care Society

page.mentor_intro: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) is a critical neurological emergency requiring emergent non-contrast head CT, early aneurysm securement (<24h), enteral nimodipine neuroprotection, and proactive surveillance for delayed cerebral ischemia.

teaching_points.claim: AHA/ASA 2023 guidelines recommend oral nimodipine (60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days) initiated immediately upon diagnosis; in the landmark British aneurysm nimodipine trial, nimodipine reduced cerebral infarction by 34% (p<0.001) and significantly reduced poor neurological outcomes.

In the landmark International Subarachnoid Aneurysm Trial (ISAT) of 2,143 patients, endovascular coiling of ruptured intracranial aneurysms amenable to both techniques produced significantly higher 1-year independent survival (23.5% dependent/dead vs 30.9% with surgical clipping; absolute risk reduction 7.4%; p=0.0001).

Emergency aneurysm repair (coiling or clipping) should be performed as early as feasible (within 24 hours of rupture) to eliminate the catastrophic ~15% early re-bleeding risk, which carries an associated mortality exceeding 70%.

Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) typically develops between days 4 and 14 post-hemorrhage; Neurocritical Care Society consensus guidelines mandate maintenance of euvolemia (avoiding prophylactic hypervolemic 'triple-H' therapy) and induced arterial hypertension with vasopressors upon clinical evidence of DCI.

topic: Neuroendocrine tumours: WHO grading G1/G2/G3, Ki-67, somatostatin receptor imaging

guidelinesKept: A common classification framework for neuroendocrine neoplasms: an update and presentation of the WHO 2022 framework

page.mentor_intro: Neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) are classified by the WHO 2022 framework into well-differentiated tumors (G1, G2, G3) based on mitotic count and Ki-67 proliferation index; functional imaging with somatostatin receptor PET-CT directs targeted somatostatin analogues and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT).

teaching_points.claim: The WHO 2022 classification stratifies well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) strictly by Ki-67 proliferation index: Grade 1 (Ki-67 <3%), Grade 2 (Ki-67 3% to 20%), and Grade 3 (Ki-67 >20%), differentiating well-differentiated G3 NETs (preserved DAXX/ATRX, intact RB1/TP53) from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NEC: small cell or large cell, TP53/RB1 mutated).

In the landmark phase 3 NETTER-1 trial, 177Lu-dotatate peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) combined with octreotide LAR in patients with advanced progressive midgut NETs significantly reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 79% (HR 0.21; p<0.001) compared with high-dose octreotide LAR alone.

Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) PET imaging using 68Ga-DOTATATE, 68Ga-DOTATOC, or 64Cu-DOTATATE demonstrates diagnostic sensitivity >95% and specificity >90%, outperforming conventional 111In-pentetreotide Octreoscan and CT in detecting occult primary sites and distant metastases.

ESMO guidelines establish long-acting somatostatin analogues (octreotide LAR 30 mg or lanreotide autogel 120 mg every 4 weeks) as first-line antiproliferative and antisecretory therapy for advanced, unresectable, well-differentiated G1/G2 gastrointestinal and pancreatic NETs.

topic: Neuromuscular blocking agents in the ICU: indications and monitoring

guidelinesKept: Clinical practice guidelines for sustained neuromuscular blockade in the adult critically ill patient

page.mentor_intro: Neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) in the intensive care unit improve chest wall compliance and eliminate patient-ventilator dyssynchrony in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), requiring structured indications, deep sedation, and quantitative peripheral nerve train-of-four monitoring.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark ACURASYS trial by Papazian and colleagues, early continuous infusion of the non-depolarizing NMBA cisatracurium for 48 hours in severe ARDS (PaO2/FiO2 <150 mmHg) significantly improved 90-day survival (adjusted HR 0.68; p=0.04) and increased ventilator-free days.

Conversely, the large multicenter ROSE trial evaluated early neuromuscular blockade combined with modern high PEEP lung-protective ventilation and deep sedation, finding no significant difference in 90-day mortality (42.5% vs 42.8%) compared with light sedation and neuromuscular blockade used only as rescue.

Clinical guidelines recommend reserving continuous NMBA infusions for severe ARDS with refractory hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 <150), persistent severe patient-ventilator dyssynchrony, high plateau pressures >30 cmH2O, or shivering during targeted temperature management.

Prolonged neuromuscular blockade is a major contributor to ICU-acquired weakness (critical illness myopathy and neuropathy); monitoring mandates clinical assessment paired with peripheral nerve stimulation (train-of-four [TOF] goal of 1 to 2 twitches) and daily cessation trials.

page.mentor_intro: Neuromuscular respiratory failure results from diaphragmatic and intercostal muscle pump exhaustion in conditions such as Guillain-Barré syndrome and myasthenic crisis, demanding serial bedside spirometry and early elective endotracheal intubation before hypercapnic arrest occurs.

teaching_points.claim: The clinical '20/30/40 rule' validated by Lawn and colleagues identifies impending ventilatory failure in Guillain-Barré syndrome and myasthenia gravis: forced vital capacity (FVC) <20 mL/kg, maximum inspiratory pressure (MIP/NIF) less negative than -30 cmH2O, or maximum expiratory pressure (MEP) <40 cmH2O mandates ICU admission and elective intubation.

Pulse oximetry and arterial blood gases are dangerously insensitive late indicators; normal oxygen saturation is maintained until hypercapnic respiratory arrest is imminent, making serial upright and supine vital capacity the essential bedside monitoring tool.

Diaphragmatic weakness is clinically signaled by paradoxical abdominal inward movement during inspiration in the supine position and an acute drop in forced vital capacity >20% when moving from an upright sitting to a supine position.

In acute myasthenic crisis, immediate definitive disease-modifying therapy consists of therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX) or intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days); acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (pyridostigmine) should be temporarily discontinued in intubated patients to avoid excessive tracheobronchial secretions.

topic: neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder biologic therapy

guidelinesKept: International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder

page.mentor_intro: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a severe autoimmune astrocytopathy mediated by pathogenic autoantibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG); modern targeted biologics (eculizumab, satralizumab, inebilizumab) dramatically suppress attacks and prevent cumulative disability.

teaching_points.claim: In the randomized phase 3 PREVENT trial by Pittock and colleagues, terminal complement C5 inhibition with intravenous eculizumab reduced the adjudicated relapse rate by 94% (HR 0.06; 95% CI 0.02-0.20; p<0.001) in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD.

The phase 3 SAkuraSky trial demonstrated that the subcutaneous IL-6 receptor antagonist satralizumab added to baseline immunosuppression significantly reduced the risk of relapse by 62% overall (HR 0.38) and by 79% in AQP4-IgG-seropositive patients (HR 0.21; p=0.001).

In the phase 3 N-MOmentum trial, inebilizumab (humanized monoclonal antibody targeting CD19 to deplete both B cells and antibody-secreting plasmablasts) reduced the risk of NMOSD attack by 73% (HR 0.27; p<0.0001) and reduced worsening of disability.

Traditional multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapies (interferon-beta, fingolimod, natalizumab) are ineffective and can trigger catastrophic relapses in NMOSD, underscoring the critical requirement for early AQP4-IgG serological testing.

topic: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (NMOSD): AQP4-IgG, long extensive transverse myelitis

guidelinesKept: International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder

page.mentor_intro: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is an autoimmune demyelinating central nervous system astrocytopathy driven by complement-activating autoantibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP4), classically presenting with longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM), severe optic neuritis, and area postrema syndrome.

teaching_points.claim: According to the 2015 International Panel for NMO Diagnosis (IPND) criteria, NMOSD with AQP4-IgG requires at least 1 core clinical characteristic: optic neuritis, acute myelitis (LETM), area postrema syndrome (intractable hiccups, nausea, vomiting), acute brainstem syndrome, narcolepsy/diencephalic syndrome, or symptomatic cerebral syndrome.

Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) is the pathognomonic spinal MRI hallmark of NMOSD, defined as a contiguous intramedullary T2-hyperintense spinal cord lesion spanning 3 or more vertebral segments, typically involving the central gray matter with cord swelling.

Lennon and colleagues demonstrated that NMO-IgG autoantibodies selectively target the aquaporin-4 water channel localized on astrocytic foot processes at the blood-brain barrier, triggering complement activation, astrocyte lysis, secondary oligodendrocyte death, and severe necrotic demyelination.

The area postrema syndrome occurs in up to 12% of presentations and is characterized by episodes of intractable nausea, vomiting, or hiccups lasting >48 hours without gastrointestinal etiology, caused by localized AQP4-IgG-mediated inflammation in the floor of the fourth ventricle.

page.mentor_intro: Neuropathic leg and foot ulcers result from sensorimotor and autonomic diabetic peripheral neuropathy, characterized by painless ulceration over high-pressure plantar prominences, requiring structured offloading (total contact casting), sharp surgical debridement, and osteomyelitis exclusion.

teaching_points.claim: According to the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF) guidelines, loss of protective sensation (LOPS) confirmed by an inability to feel the 10-gram Semmes-Weinstein monofilament on plantar surfaces is the primary predisposing cause of neuropathic foot ulceration.

The probe-to-bone (PTB) test is an essential clinical assessment: in a prospective validation by Grayson and colleagues, palpating hard gritty bone with a sterile metallic probe in an infected ulcer had a positive predictive value of 89% for underlying osteomyelitis, guiding the requirement for plain radiography, MRI, or bone biopsy.

IWGDF guidelines establish non-removable knee-high offloading devices (total contact cast [TCC] or non-removable knee-high walker) as the first-choice standard of care for healing plantar neuropathic forefoot and midfoot ulcers, significantly accelerating healing rates compared to removable therapeutic shoes.

Autonomic neuropathy contributes to ulcer pathogenesis through anhidrosis (causing dry, cracked, hyperkeratotic fissures) and sympathetic denervation, opening arteriovenous shunts that produce bounding foot pulses in warm, insensate, high-risk feet.

page.mentor_intro: Neuropathic pain is caused by a lesion or disease of the somatosensory nervous system, characterized by spontaneous burning pain, hyperalgesia, and allodynia, treated according to evidence-based consensus guidelines prioritizing gabapentinoids, SNRIs, and tricyclic antidepressants while strictly limiting opioids.

teaching_points.claim: In the NeuPSIG / International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) systematic review and meta-analysis by Finnerup and colleagues, three drug classes were established as first-line Level A evidence for neuropathic pain: gabapentinoids (pregabalin, gabapentin), serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (duloxetine, venlafaxine), and tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline, nortriptyline).

Gabapentinoids (pregabalin 150-600 mg daily, gabapentin 900-3600 mg daily) bind the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing presynaptic excitatory neurotransmitter release with a number needed to treat (NNT) of approximately 7.2 for >=50% pain reduction.

Duloxetine (60-120 mg once daily) selectively inhibits presynaptic reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline, enhancing descending inhibitory pain pathways with proven efficacy across painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (NNT ~6.4) and central neuropathic pain without causing anticholinergic side effects.

Tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline 10-75 mg at bedtime) exhibit the lowest NNT (~3.6) across peripheral neuropathic pain conditions, but carry significant anticholinergic adverse effects, sedation, and cardiotoxicity (QTc prolongation, fatal ventricular arrhythmias in overdose) requiring baseline ECG screening.

topic: Neurosarcoidosis: cranial neuropathies, meningeal enhancement, CSF profile

guidelinesKept: Definition and Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Neurosarcoidosis: from the Neurosarcoidosis Consortium Consensus Group

page.mentor_intro: Neurosarcoidosis is a non-caseating granulomatous disorder of the nervous system affecting 5-10% of systemic sarcoidosis patients, characteristically manifesting as cranial neuropathies, basilar leptomeningitis, or hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, diagnosed by consensus criteria and treated with corticosteroids and targeted TNF inhibitors.

teaching_points.claim: According to the Neurosarcoidosis Consortium Consensus Group criteria by Stern and colleagues, diagnosis is classified into definite (positive nervous system biopsy), probable (clinical/MRI features with positive extra-neural biopsy), and possible neurosarcoidosis (suggestive presentation after excluding alternative etiologies).

Cranial neuropathies represent the most common neurological manifestation (seen in 50-70% of cases), with facial nerve palsy (cranial nerve VII, frequently bilateral or sequential) being the classic presentation, followed by optic neuropathy (cranial nerve II).

In refractory or severe neurosarcoidosis, Gelfand and colleagues demonstrated that the anti-TNF monoclonal antibody infliximab achieved complete or partial radiographic and clinical remission in over 75% of patients who failed high-dose corticosteroids and conventional immunosuppressants.

Cerebrospinal fluid examination characteristically reveals elevated protein (>1.0 g/L), lymphocytic pleocytosis, hypoglycorrhachia in up to 20%, and unique CSF oligoclonal bands in 30-50%, while contrast-enhanced brain/spine MRI shows nodular basilar leptomeningeal enhancement.

topic: Neutropenic sepsis: MASCC score, empirical piperacillin-tazobactam, antifungal escalation

guidelinesKept: Outpatient management of fever and neutropenia in adults with cancer: ASCO/IDSA clinical practice guideline update
Clinical practice guideline for the use of antimicrobial agents in neutropenic patients with cancer: 2010 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America

page.mentor_intro: Neutropenic sepsis is a medical emergency defined by fever (>=38.3 C or >=38.0 C sustained for 1 hour) and an absolute neutrophil count <0.5 x 10^9/L, requiring rapid MASCC risk stratification and immediate intravenous empirical antipseudomonal beta-lactam administration within 1 hour.

teaching_points.claim: The Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer (MASCC) risk index score stratifies neutropenic fever: a score >=21 identifies low-risk patients with <5% risk of severe medical complications, who may be eligible for step-down oral outpatient therapy (ciprofloxacin plus amoxicillin-clavulanate).

IDSA and ASCO guidelines mandate a door-to-antibiotic time of <60 minutes; immediate empirical broad-spectrum monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6h, cefepime 2 g q8h, or meropenem 1 g q8h) is the Class I standard of care.

Vancomycin should not be initiated routinely in empirical therapy unless specific indications exist: hemodynamic instability/septic shock, suspected catheter-related bloodstream infection, known colonization with MRSA, skin/soft-tissue infection, or pneumonia.

In patients with persistent or recrudescent fever after 4 to 7 days of broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy and expected neutropenia lasting >7 days, empirical antifungal therapy with voriconazole, liposomal amphotericin B, or an echinocandin is indicated to cover invasive aspergillosis and candidiasis.

page.mentor_intro: Airway management in emergency and critical care settings has evolved with modern video laryngoscopes, second-generation supraglottic airway devices, and rigid bougies, which significantly enhance first-pass intubation success and reduce hypoxemic and aspiration complications.

teaching_points.claim: In the multicenter randomized DEVICE trial evaluating 1,417 critically ill adults, video laryngoscopy significantly increased first-pass intubation success to 85.1% compared with 70.8% for direct laryngoscopy (absolute difference 14.2%; p<0.001), without increasing procedural complications.

In the randomized BOUGIE trial by Driver and colleagues, using an endotracheal tube introducer (bougie) on the first attempt significantly increased first-pass intubation success (98% vs 87%; p<0.001) compared with an endotracheal tube with stylet in patients with anticipated difficult airways.

Difficult Airway Society (DAS) guidelines mandate that second-generation supraglottic airway devices (SADs, such as i-gel and LMA Supreme) are the rescue devices of choice for 'cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate' (CICO) scenarios; their gastric drainage channels isolate the airway and protect against pulmonary aspiration.

The Fourth National Audit Project (NAP4) identified that failure to use capnography was a major contributing factor in over 70% of ICU and emergency airway-related deaths, establishing continuous waveform capnography as a non-negotiable mandatory standard for all tracheal intubations.

topic: New-onset seizure in adults: diagnostic workup, EEG patterns, imaging

guidelinesKept: ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy

page.mentor_intro: A new-onset unprovoked seizure in an adult requires emergency exclusion of acute metabolic, toxic, or structural etiologies, followed by dedicated neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and recurrence risk stratification to guide anti-seizure medication (ASM) initiation under the ILAE 2014 definition of epilepsy.

teaching_points.claim: According to the ILAE official definition, epilepsy is diagnosed after a single unprovoked seizure if the individual has an enduring predisposition to further seizures, defined as an estimated recurrence risk >=60% over the next 10 years (e.g., significant epileptogenic structural MRI lesion or clear epileptiform discharges on EEG).

AAN and AES guidelines state that unprovoked first seizure recurrence risk is highest in the first 2 years (21-45%); immediate initiation of anti-seizure medication reduces 2-year recurrence risk by approximately 35% compared to deferred therapy, although it does not alter long-term remission rates.

In the SANAD II multicenter randomized trial, lamotrigine was superior to levetiracetam and zonisamide as first-line monotherapy for newly diagnosed focal epilepsy, demonstrating significantly higher treatment success (12-month remission) and superior cost-effectiveness.

Neuroimaging standards require high-resolution brain MRI utilizing an epilepsy-dedicated protocol (including 3D volumetric T1, T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis, and 3D fluid-attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR]) to detect subtle cortical dysplasias, mesial temporal sclerosis, or low-grade neoplasms.

topic: Nitrate therapy: GTN, isosorbide mononitrate, tolerance, combination use

guidelinesKept: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of chronic coronary syndromes

page.mentor_intro: Organic nitrates (glyceryl trinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, isosorbide dinitrate) provide venodilation, reduce myocardial preload and coronary vasospasm, but develop rapid tolerance requiring an asymmetric 10-14 hour nitrate-free interval, and are strictly contraindicated with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.

teaching_points.claim: In a randomized clinical trial by Parker and colleagues, continuous round-the-clock administration of nitrates induced complete loss of anti-anginal and hemodynamic efficacy within 24-48 hours (nitrate tolerance), which was prevented by an asymmetric eccentric dosing schedule (e.g., isosorbide mononitrate at 08:00 and 15:00) providing a 10-14 hour daily nitrate-free interval.

Molecular mechanisms of nitrate tolerance involve depletion of mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH-2, which bioactivates nitroglycerin), uncoupling of endothelial nitric oxide synthase, increased reactive oxygen species generation, and neurohormonal activation.

Co-administration of organic nitrates with phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5) inhibitors (sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil) causes synergistic accumulation of cyclic GMP, resulting in catastrophic, refractory, life-threatening hypotension and myocardial infarction; nitrates must be withheld for >=24 hours after sildenafil/vardenafil and >=48 hours after tadalafil.

ESC guidelines recommend short-acting sublingual glyceryl trinitrate (GTN tablet or spray) as first-line Class I therapy for immediate relief of acute angina symptoms and pre-effort prophylaxis, while oral long-acting nitrates are secondary add-on anti-anginal agents when beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers are insufficient or contraindicated.

topic: nivolumab ipilimumab advanced melanoma overall survival

page.mentor_intro: Combined immune checkpoint blockade with nivolumab (anti-PD-1) plus ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4) fundamentally revolutionized the treatment landscape of advanced and metastatic melanoma. Landmark data from the phase 3 CheckMate 067 trial demonstrated durable long-term overall survival benefits with dual immunotherapy compared to monotherapy, albeit at the cost of significantly higher rates of grade 3-4 immune-related adverse events.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark phase 3 CheckMate 067 trial, combination therapy with nivolumab (1 mg/kg) plus ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) achieved a median overall survival of 72.1 months in previously untreated advanced melanoma, compared with 36.9 months with nivolumab monotherapy and 19.9 months with ipilimumab alone.

The long-term landmark analysis confirmed a 6.5-year overall survival rate of 49% for nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 42% for nivolumab alone, establishing durable disease control even after treatment discontinuation.

Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 59% of patients receiving nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to 21% receiving nivolumab monotherapy and 28% receiving ipilimumab alone, most commonly colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, and endocrinopathies.

Subgroup analysis showed that while dual checkpoint inhibition confers superior progression-free survival across BRAF-mutant and wild-type subgroups, patients with PD-L1 expression >=1% derive significant benefit from nivolumab monotherapy, whereas PD-L1 negative tumors show substantial incremental survival benefit with dual blockade.

page.mentor_intro: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)—recently reclassified in consensus nomenclatures as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)—represents the hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome. Risk stratification focuses on distinguishing simple steatosis from metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and identifying advanced hepatic fibrosis (stage F3-F4), which serves as the primary determinant of long-term liver-related morbidity and all-cause mortality.

teaching_points.claim: Non-invasive fibrosis scoring systems, particularly the FIB-4 index (incorporating age, AST, ALT, and platelet count) and NAFLD Fibrosis Score (NFS), serve as the first-line primary care screening tools to rule out advanced fibrosis (FIB-4 <1.30 having a negative predictive value >90%).

Hepatic fibrosis stage (F2-F4), rather than the degree of steatosis or histologic inflammatory activity, is the sole histologic parameter independently associated with overall mortality, liver transplantation, and hepatic decompensation.

Vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE / FibroScan) with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) provides quantitative measurement of liver stiffness (kPa) and steatosis, where liver stiffness <8.0 kPa effectively excludes advanced fibrosis.

EASL-EASD-EASO clinical practice guidelines recommend screening all patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, or metabolic syndrome for liver steatosis and advanced fibrosis using serum biomarkers followed by transient elastography.

page.mentor_intro: Management of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD/MASLD) requires a multidisciplinary framework targeting metabolic drivers, cardiovascular risk reduction, and prevention of hepatic decompensation. Sustained weight reduction through lifestyle modification forms the cornerstone of therapy, while structured metabolic interventions—including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors—address shared cardiometabolic pathophysiology.

teaching_points.claim: Dose-dependent lifestyle-induced weight loss correlates directly with histologic improvement: >=5% weight loss reduces hepatic steatosis, >=7% achieves MASH resolution, and >=10% induces regression or stabilization of liver fibrosis.

Cardiovascular disease—not end-stage liver disease—is the leading cause of death in patients with NAFLD across all fibrosis stages, mandating aggressive lipid-lowering therapy with statins, which are proven safe and hepatoprotective in steatotic liver disease.

The Mediterranean diet is recommended by international clinical guidelines as the primary nutritional model for NAFLD, demonstrating reduction in hepatic steatosis and improved insulin sensitivity independent of caloric restriction.

Bariatric metabolic surgery yields durable resolution of steatohepatitis in over 80% of patients and fibrosis improvement in over 30% of morbidly obese individuals with biopsy-proven MASH at 5-year follow-up.

page.mentor_intro: The bidirectional relationship between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and peripheral insulin resistance positions hepatic steatosis as both a consequence and driver of the metabolic syndrome. Clinical triage relies heavily on sequential non-invasive fibrosis testing (FIB-4 score followed by elastography) to detect advanced fibrosis in at-risk diabetic and obese populations before irreversible cirrhotic complications emerge.

teaching_points.claim: Peripheral and hepatic insulin resistance impairs adipocyte lipolysis suppression, delivering an excessive flux of free fatty acids to hepatocytes and driving lipotoxicity, mitochondrial oxidative stress, and progressive inflammation.

The FIB-4 index uses age, AST, ALT, and platelet count to calculate a fibrosis risk score; values <1.30 (<2.0 in age >65) exclude advanced fibrosis with >90% negative predictive value, while values >2.67 indicate high probability of stage F3-F4 fibrosis.

For patients in the indeterminate FIB-4 zone (1.30 to 2.67), international consensus guidelines mandate secondary risk stratification with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) or enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF) blood testing.
Screening for NAFLD in type 2 diabetic cohorts reveals advanced fibrosis (>=F3) in up to 15-20% of patients despite entirely normal serum aminotransferase levels.

page.mentor_intro: The pharmacotherapeutic pipeline for nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH/MASH) has accelerated rapidly from off-label repurposed agents (pioglitazone, vitamin E) to targeted, liver-directed small molecules and metabolic incretin dual/triple co-agonists. In early 2024, resmetirom (a liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) became the first FDA-approved therapeutic specifically indicated for non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis.

teaching_points.claim: In the pivotal phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH trial, resmetirom (80 mg and 100 mg daily) achieved both primary endpoints: MASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis in 25.9-29.9% of patients (vs 9.7% placebo) and fibrosis improvement of >=1 stage with no worsening of NAFLD activity score in 24.2-25.9% (vs 14.2% placebo).

Pioglitazone (30-45 mg daily) improves insulin resistance and significantly improves steatohepatitis and fibrosis in patients with and without type 2 diabetes in randomized clinical trials, but carries side effects of weight gain, fluid retention, and osteopenia.

Vitamin E (800 IU daily of alpha-tocopherol) improves steatosis and lobular inflammation in non-diabetic adults with biopsy-proven MASH as shown in the PIVENS trial, but lacks proven efficacy in diabetes or cirrhotic patients and has raised prostate cancer and hemorrhagic stroke concerns.

Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists such as semaglutide and dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists like tirzepatide achieve potent MASH resolution (59% in phase 2 trials) primarily mediated by substantial metabolic weight loss, with emerging evidence of antifibrotic activity.

topic: Non-functioning pituitary adenoma: chiasmal compression, surveillance vs surgery

guidelinesKept: Management of nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline

page.mentor_intro: Non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPAs) are benign epithelial neoplasms of adenohypophyseal origin that do not cause biochemical hormonal hypersecretion. Clinical presentation typically involves 'mass-effect' symptoms—most notably chiasmal compression causing bitemporal hemianopsia, cranial neuropathies, or secondary hypopituitarism—dictating whether patients require urgent endoscopic transsphenoidal surgical decompression or conservative MRI surveillance.

teaching_points.claim: Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgical resection is the first-line treatment for NFPAs causing optic chiasm compression, visual field deficits (classic bitemporal hemianopsia), or acute pituitary apoplexy, achieving visual field improvement in >80% of symptomatic patients.

Asymptomatic macroadenomas (>10 mm) without visual compromise and incidental microadenomas (<10 mm) are safely managed with active surveillance via serial pituitary MRI (at 6 and 12 months, then annually for 3 years) and periodic visual perimetry.

Complete baseline endocrine evaluation is mandatory in all NFPAs to detect subclinical hypopituitarism (assessing 8 AM cortisol, free T4, TSH, prolactin, IGF-1, LH/FSH, and sex steroids) and to exclude prolactinoma, which responds to dopamine agonists.

Mild hyperprolactinemia (<100-150 ng/mL or <2000-3000 mU/L) in NFPA represents the 'stalk effect' (loss of hypothalamic dopamine inhibition due to infundibular compression) and does not signify a macroprolactinoma, which typically exhibits prolactin levels >250 ng/mL.

guidelinesKept: Recommendations for the use of biologic agents for the treatment of noninfectious uveitis

page.mentor_intro: Noninfectious uveitis comprises an etiologically heterogeneous group of sight-threatening intraocular inflammatory disorders affecting the anterior, intermediate, posterior, or panuveal tracts. In patients with active noninfectious intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis who fail or are intolerant to systemic corticosteroids and conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (cDMARDs), biologic therapies targeting TNF-alpha (specifically adalimumab) provide potent, steroid-sparing disease control.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark phase 3 VISUAL-1 trial, adalimumab significantly delayed time to treatment failure and reduced the risk of uveitic flare (hazard ratio 0.50) compared to placebo in patients with active noninfectious intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis despite corticosteroid therapy.

The companion phase 3 VISUAL-2 trial demonstrated that adalimumab maintained remission and reduced treatment failure rates (hazard ratio 0.57) during mandatory steroid taper in patients with inactive, quiescent noninfectious uveitis.

Adalimumab is the only biologic therapy with FDA and EMA approval for noninfectious intermediate, posterior, and panuveitis in adults and pediatric patients (aged >=2 years with chronic anterior uveitis associated with JIA).

Rigorous pre-treatment screening for latent tuberculosis (IGRA/PPD and chest radiograph), hepatitis B, and demyelinating disease (multiple sclerosis) is strictly mandatory prior to anti-TNF initiation, as TNF inhibitors can provoke catastrophic CNS demyelination.

topic: Noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure

guidelinesKept: Official ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines: noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure

page.mentor_intro: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV)—encompassing bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP) and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)—is an indispensable life-saving modality for select etiologies of acute respiratory failure (ARF). Evidence robustly supports NIV in acute hypercapnic exacerbations of COPD and cardiogenic pulmonary edema, while its application in acute hypoxemic de novo respiratory failure (e.g., severe ARDS) demands rigorous caution due to the catastrophic mortality risk associated with delayed endotracheal intubation.

teaching_points.claim: ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines establish strong recommendations for NIV in acute hypercapnic respiratory failure due to COPD exacerbation (pH <=7.35, PaCO2 >45 mmHg) and cardiogenic pulmonary edema, where it reduces intubation rates, hospital stay, and in-hospital mortality.

In cardiogenic pulmonary edema, both CPAP and BiPAP rapidly improve oxygenation and dyspnea while unloading left ventricular afterload, with neither modality showing superiority over the other in large randomized multi-center trials (3CPO trial).

In acute hypoxemic non-hypercapnic respiratory failure (e.g., severe ARDS or pneumonia), NIV failure rates approach 50%; high tidal volumes (>9.5 mL/kg predicted body weight) under NIV predict imminent failure and generate patient-self-inflicted lung injury (P-SILI).

Absolute contraindications to NIV include cardiac or respiratory arrest, severe encephalopathy (Glasgow Coma Scale <8, with exception of reversible hypercapnic coma), hemodynamic instability refractory to vasopressors, facial trauma/burns, and high aspiration risk.

topic: Noninvasive ventilation for COPD hypercapnic failure

guidelinesKept: Official ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines: noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure
British Thoracic Society/Intensive Care Society Guideline for the Ventilatory Management of Acute Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure in Adults

page.mentor_intro: Acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF) secondary to acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is the definitive, gold-standard indication for noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV). When applied promptly to patients with respiratory acidosis (pH <=7.35 and PaCO2 >45 mmHg) refractory to standard medical management, NPPV offloads fatigued respiratory muscles, prevents endotracheal intubation, and slashes inpatient mortality by over 50%.

teaching_points.claim: Cochrane meta-analyses and BTS/ICS guidelines demonstrate that NPPV in COPD hypercapnic failure reduces the risk of endotracheal intubation by 65% and reduces relative in-hospital mortality by 54% compared to standard medical therapy alone.

Initial NPPV ventilator settings typically employ spontaneous/timed (S/T) bilevel mode with inspiratory positive airway pressure (IPAP) of 10-12 cm H2O and expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) of 4-5 cm H2O, titrating IPAP upward by 2-3 cm H2O to achieve a target tidal volume of 6-8 mL/kg and clinical relief.

Repeat arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis is mandatory after 1-2 hours of NPPV: a failure of pH to improve or a worsening acidosis/hypercapnia strongly predicts NPPV failure and mandates timely endotracheal intubation.

Even in patients presenting with severe hypercapnic encephalopathy (GCS <11), a closely monitored trial of NPPV in an intensive care environment is safe and often rapidly reverses encephalopathy as CO2 clearance improves, avoiding mechanical ventilation.

guidelinesKept: Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: ASCO Guideline Rapid Recommendation Update

page.mentor_intro: Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) / programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) axis have transformed the therapeutic paradigm of advanced and metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In patients without actionable oncogenic driver alterations (e.g., EGFR, ALK, ROS1), monotherapy with pembrolizumab or atezolizumab is the preferred first-line standard for high PD-L1 expressors (TPS >=50%), whereas chemoimmunotherapy combinations provide survival superiority in tumors with low (<50%) or negative (<1%) PD-L1 expression.

teaching_points.claim: In the landmark KEYNOTE-024 trial, pembrolizumab monotherapy significantly improved overall survival compared to platinum-doublet chemotherapy (median OS 30.0 vs 14.2 months, HR 0.63) in untreated advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) >=50% lacking EGFR/ALK aberrations.

In patients with metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC regardless of PD-L1 expression, the KEYNOTE-189 trial demonstrated that adding pembrolizumab to pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy significantly prolonged overall survival (12-month OS 69.2% vs 49.4%, HR 0.49).

In metastatic squamous NSCLC, the KEYNOTE-407 trial confirmed that pembrolizumab combined with carboplatin and paclitaxel/nab-paclitaxel produced significant overall survival benefits (median OS 15.9 vs 11.3 months, HR 0.64) across all PD-L1 strata.

Before initiating checkpoint immunotherapy in advanced NSCLC, comprehensive molecular biomarker testing for targetable driver mutations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, RET, MET exon 14, KRAS G12C) is mandatory, as EGFR/ALK-positive tumors exhibit low response rates to single-agent immunotherapy and heightened risk of severe immune pneumonitis.

page.mentor_intro: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) is a distinct idiopathic or autoimmune-associated interstitial lung disease characterised by homogeneous alveolar wall inflammation or expansion, contrasting with the patchy, heterogeneous subpleural honeycombing typical of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP/IPF). NSIP carries a markedly superior prognosis compared to IPF, exhibits prominent responsiveness to systemic immunosuppression, and frequently serves as the pulmonary sentinel manifestation of systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis, or undifferentiated connective tissue disease.

teaching_points.claim: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) in NSIP characteristically shows bilateral, symmetric ground-glass opacities and fine reticulation with lower lobe and subpleural sparing, whereas honeycombing is characteristically absent or minimal.

Histopathologically, NSIP is categorized into cellular and fibrotic variants; cellular NSIP consists of mild-to-moderate chronic interstitial inflammation without significant collagen remodeling, conferring an exceptional 5-year survival (>90%).

First-line pharmacotherapy for symptomatic or deteriorating NSIP consists of systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day) often combined with steroid-sparing immunosuppressants (mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, or azathioprine).

In patients with progressive fibrosing NSIP despite immunomodulatory therapy, the phase 3 INBUILD trial demonstrated that the tyrosine kinase inhibitor nintedanib significantly slowed the annual rate of decline in forced vital capacity (FVC).
